question: An agent must summarize 10 independent documents; which approach minimizes latency?

options.text: Issue 10 concurrent calls (one per document) then combine the summaries
Process the documents sequentially in a single conversation
Concatenate all 10 into one prompt and ask for 10 summaries
Using an evaluator optimization loop per document

explanation: The ten documents are independent, so no call depends on another's output. Issuing ten concurrent requests (the parallelization workflow, sectioning variant) makes wall-clock latency roughly that of the slowest single call, and a final step combines the summaries. Sequential processing (B) adds the latencies together and also drags growing context along. One giant prompt (C) produces ten summaries serially in a single generation, so output time is the sum, and long-context quality can degrade. An evaluator-optimizer loop (D) adds extra iterations per document, increasing latency and is meant for quality refinement, not speed.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un agente debe resumir 10 documentos independientes; ¿Qué enfoque minimiza la latencia?

options.text: Realice 10 llamadas simultáneas (una por documento) y luego combine los resúmenes
Procesa los documentos de forma secuencial en una sola conversación
Concatene los 10 en un mensaje y solicite 10 resúmenes
Uso de un bucle de optimización del evaluador por documento

es.explanation: Paralelizar tareas independientes es la forma estándar de reducir la latencia.

question: Which signal most strongly indicates that an agentic design has become too complex?

options.text: It uses more than one tool
Failures are difficult to attribute to a specific step and behavior cannot be reproduced
It uses a system prompt
It streams responses

explanation: Anthropic recommends the simplest solution that works and adding complexity only when it demonstrably helps. The warning sign is loss of observability: when you cannot attribute a failure to a specific step or reproduce behavior, the design has more moving parts than you can reason about, so simplify. Using several tools (A) is normal and often required. A system prompt (C) is standard practice for any agent. Streaming (D) is a delivery mechanism that affects latency/UX and says nothing about design complexity.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Qué señal indica con más fuerza que un diseño agencial se ha vuelto demasiado complejo?

options.text: Utiliza más de una herramienta.
Los fallos son difíciles de atribuir a un paso específico y el comportamiento no se puede reproducir.
Utiliza un indicador del sistema.
Transmite respuestas

es.explanation: Si no puede rastrear una falla en un paso o reproducir un error, es probable que el sistema sea demasiado complejo.

question: What is the purpose of an explicit plan or task list artifact maintained by long-running agents?

options.text: It replaces the need for tools
It externalizes goals and progress so they survive context compaction and keep the agent oriented
It reduces the API rate limits
It guarantees the agent finishes

explanation: Long-running agents outlast a single context window, and compaction or truncation can drop earlier goals and progress. Keeping an explicit plan or task list in external state (a file, a to-do tool, memory) externalizes goals and progress so the agent can re-read them after compaction and stay oriented. It does not replace tools (A); it is usually maintained via tools. It has no effect on API rate limits (C), which are server-side quotas. It cannot guarantee completion (D), only improve the odds by reducing drift.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál es el propósito de un plan explícito o un artefacto de lista de tareas mantenido por agentes de larga duración?

options.text: Reemplaza la necesidad de herramientas.
Externaliza los objetivos y el progreso para que sobrevivan a la compactación del contexto y mantengan al agente orientado.
Reduce los límites de tasa API.
Garantiza que el agente termine

es.explanation: Los agentes de largo plazo necesitan un estado externo duradero para evitar perder el rumbo durante las restricciones de la ventana de contexto.

question: Which are valid reasons to insert a deterministic code step between two model calls in a workflow? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To validate that the first call's output conforms to the expected schema
To perform a calculation or lookup that code does more reliably than a model
To transform or filter data into the shape the next prompt expects
To make the workflow non-deterministic
To bypass the context window limit for the whole workflow

explanation: Workflows are valuable precisely because code and models are mixed according to strengths. Deterministic steps (gates) validate that an output matches a schema before it propagates (A), do arithmetic, lookups or database queries that code does exactly (B), and reshape or filter data into the form the next prompt needs (C). Making the workflow non-deterministic (D) is not a goal; code steps do the opposite. Bypassing the context window limit (E) is false: each model call still has its own window, and code between calls does not enlarge it (though it can trim what is passed on).

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuáles son razones válidas para insertar un paso de código determinista entre dos llamadas de modelo en un flujo de trabajo? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Para validar que el resultado de la primera llamada se ajuste al esquema esperado
Para realizar un cálculo o una búsqueda, ese código lo hace de manera más confiable que un modelo.
Para transformar o filtrar datos en la forma que espera el siguiente mensaje
Para hacer que el flujo de trabajo no sea determinista
Para omitir el límite de la ventana de contexto para todo el flujo de trabajo

es.explanation: Utilice modelos para el lenguaje y la ambigüedad, utilice código para validación, cálculo y transformación.

question: An agent repeatedly calls a tool that returns an error, ignoring the failure and trying again identically. What is missing from the design?

options.text: A larger context window
Structured, actionable error results plus a retry cap that changes strategy or escalates
A higher temperature
More tools

explanation: An agent that retries the same failing call identically is missing two things: error results the model can act on (a clear message saying what failed and what to change, returned with is_error so the model sees it) and a harness-level retry cap that forces a different strategy or escalates to a human or stops. A larger context window (A) does not change behavior, it only lets the loop run longer. Higher temperature (C) adds randomness but no information or limit. More tools (D) do not fix a loop on a failing one and can worsen tool selection.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un agente llama repetidamente a una herramienta que devuelve un error, ignora el fallo y vuelve a intentarlo de forma idéntica. ¿Qué falta en el diseño?

options.text: Una ventana de contexto más grande
Resultados de errores estructurados y procesables más un límite de reintentos que cambia la estrategia o escala
Una temperatura más alta
Más herramientas

es.explanation: Los arneses deben detectar bucles y fallas para cambiar el comportamiento en lugar de volver a intentarlo sin pensar.

question: Which describes the correct relationship between agents and tools?

options.text: The agent decides which tool to call and with what arguments; your code executes it and returns the result
The model executes tools directly against external systems
Tools call the model when they need help
Tools are executed by the Anthropic API on your behalf

explanation: In tool use the model only emits a structured request (a tool_use block with the tool name and arguments). Your code, the middleman, validates and executes it, enforces permissions, and returns a tool_result for the next model call. The model cannot run anything itself (B), so there is no direct access to external systems. Tools do not call the model (C) unless your code deliberately does so. For client tools, the Anthropic API does not execute them (D); only Anthropic-run server tools such as web search are executed by the API, which is an exception rather than the general relationship.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál describe la relación correcta entre agentes y herramientas?

options.text: El agente decide a qué herramienta llamar y con qué argumentos; tu código lo ejecuta y devuelve el resultado
El modelo ejecuta herramientas directamente contra sistemas externos.
Las herramientas llaman al modelo cuando necesitan ayuda.
Las herramientas son ejecutadas por la API de Anthropic en su nombre

es.explanation: El código actúa como intermediario seguro para la ejecución de la herramienta.

question: Which is the correct minimal set of headers for a Messages API request?

options.text: x-api-key, anthropic-version, content-type
Authorization, Accept, User-Agent
x-api-key only
anthropic-version and content-type only

explanation: The Messages API requires x-api-key (authentication), anthropic-version (e.g. 2023-06-01, pinning API behavior) and content-type: application/json. Authorization/Accept/User-Agent (B) is a generic HTTP set and Anthropic does not use Bearer auth for this endpoint. x-api-key alone (C) omits the mandatory version header, and the request is rejected. Version and content-type without a key (D) fails authentication. Official SDKs set these headers for you, but this is the minimal raw HTTP set.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es el conjunto mínimo correcto de encabezados para una solicitud de API de mensajes?

options.text: x-api-key, versión antrópica, tipo de contenido
Autorización, Aceptar, Usuario-Agente
x-api-key solamente
versión antrópica y tipo de contenido solamente

es.explanation: Estos tres encabezados son necesarios para las solicitudes de API estándar.

question: A developer receives invalid_request_error: 'tool_use IDs were found without tool_result blocks immediately after'. What went wrong?

options.text: The client failed to return a tool_result for every tool_use in the preceding assistant turn
The tool's input_schema was invalid
The API key lacks tool permissions
max_tokens was too small

explanation: The API requires that every tool_use block in an assistant turn be answered by a matching tool_result (same tool_use_id) in the very next user message, placed first in the content. This error appears when the client skipped one, for example when several parallel tool calls were made and only some results were returned, or other content was inserted in between. An invalid input_schema (B) is rejected at definition time with a different message. Missing tool permissions (C) would produce a permission/authentication error, not a message-structure error. A small max_tokens (D) causes stop_reason max_tokens, not this validation error.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Tool use (function calling)

es.question: Un desarrollador recibe invalid_request_error: 'Se encontraron ID de uso de herramienta sin bloques de resultado de herramienta inmediatamente después'. ¿Qué salió mal?

options.text: El cliente no pudo devolver un resultado de herramienta para cada uso de herramienta en el turno anterior del asistente.
El input_schema de la herramienta no era válido
La clave API carece de permisos de herramienta
max_tokens era demasiado pequeño

es.explanation: El modelo espera una respuesta por cada bloque de uso de herramientas que genera.

question: Which are appropriate ways to expose Claude functionality to a mobile application? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A backend endpoint that authenticates the user and calls Claude server-side
Server-side enforcement of per-user quotas
Streaming from the backend to the app over a WebSocket or SSE proxy
Shipping the API key in the mobile binary
Letting the app choose arbitrary model and max_tokens values

explanation: A mobile app must never hold the API key, so a backend that authenticates the user and calls Claude server-side is the right pattern (A). The backend is also where per-user quotas are enforced (B) because client-side limits can be bypassed, and it can proxy streaming to the app via SSE or WebSocket (C) to keep UX responsive. Shipping the key in the binary (D) is a critical flaw because binaries can be decompiled and the key extracted. Letting the app choose arbitrary model and max_tokens (E) lets a malicious client run up cost, so these should be fixed or validated server-side.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son las formas apropiadas de exponer la funcionalidad de Claude a una aplicación móvil? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Un punto final de backend que autentica al usuario y llama a Claude del lado del servidor
Aplicación del lado del servidor de cuotas por usuario
Transmisión desde el backend a la aplicación a través de un proxy WebSocket o SSE
Envío de la clave API en el binario móvil
Permitir que la aplicación elija un modelo arbitrario y valores max_tokens

es.explanation: Nunca exponga las claves API en el código móvil del lado del cliente; Utilice un backend seguro.

question: What does the Anthropic-ratelimit family of response headers provide?

options.text: Remaining request and token capacity plus reset timestamps for the current window
The cost of the request in currency
The model's confidence in its answer
The number of tokens remaining in the context window

explanation: The anthropic-ratelimit-* response headers (requests/tokens limit, remaining, and reset time as an RFC 3339 timestamp) report your current rate-limit capacity so clients can throttle themselves before receiving 429s. They do not report monetary cost (B); that comes from the usage object and billing tools. They carry no model confidence (C), which the API does not expose. The context window (D) is a model property tracked via usage and token counting, not by rate-limit headers.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué proporciona la familia de encabezados de respuesta Anthropic-ratelimit?

options.text: Solicitud restante y capacidad de token más marcas de tiempo de restablecimiento para la ventana actual
El costo de la solicitud en moneda.
La confianza del modelo en su respuesta.
La cantidad de tokens que quedan en la ventana contextual.

es.explanation: Estos encabezados ayudan a los clientes a administrar sus tasas de solicitudes para mantenerse dentro de los límites.

question: Which describes the correct handling of a partially received stream when the connection drops?

options.text: Treat the partial content as complete and continue
Detect the incomplete stream, discard or mark the partial result, and retry the request with backoff
Ask the model to continue from where it stopped in a new request without any context
Ignore the error since streaming is best-effort

explanation: A dropped stream leaves a truncated response: a message_stop event (and a stop_reason in message_delta) was never received, so the content is incomplete and may even be cut mid-JSON or mid-tool-call. The robust handling is to detect the missing completion event, discard or flag the partial result, and retry with exponential backoff (or resume with the partial content as an assistant prefix where supported). Treating it as complete (A) risks acting on corrupted output. Continuing in a new request without context (C) loses what was already produced and the model cannot know where it stopped. Ignoring the error (D) hides failures; streaming is not best-effort.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe el manejo correcto de una transmisión parcialmente recibida cuando se cae la conexión?

options.text: Trate el contenido parcial como completo y continúe
Detecte la secuencia incompleta, descarte o marque el resultado parcial y vuelva a intentar la solicitud con retroceso
Pídale al modelo que continúe desde donde se detuvo en una nueva solicitud sin ningún contexto.
Ignore el error ya que la transmisión es el mejor esfuerzo

es.explanation: Verifique siempre la finalización mediante el evento de detención; Manejar con gracia las respuestas incompletas.

question: Which is a correct statement about the system parameter and prompt caching together?

options.text: A large, stable system prompt is an ideal candidate for a cache breakpoint
The system prompt cannot be cached
Caching requires the system prompt to be empty
Caching the system prompt prevents tool use

explanation: Prompt caching works by placing a cache_control breakpoint, and the cached prefix is made of tools, then system, then messages. A large, stable system prompt is the ideal candidate: it is identical across requests, so later calls read it at a fraction of the input price and with lower latency (subject to minimum cacheable length). The statement that it cannot be cached (B) is false; system blocks accept cache_control. Caching does not require an empty system prompt (C), and it does not interfere with tool use (D); tool definitions can themselves be cached too.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Prompt caching

es.question: ¿Cuál es una afirmación correcta sobre el parámetro del sistema y el almacenamiento en caché de mensajes juntos?

options.text: Un indicador del sistema grande y estable es un candidato ideal para un punto de interrupción de la caché
El indicador del sistema no se puede almacenar en caché
El almacenamiento en caché requiere que el indicador del sistema esté vacío
El almacenamiento en caché del indicador del sistema evita el uso de herramientas

es.explanation: El contenido estable y de gran tamaño es perfecto para el almacenamiento en caché.

question: A team must support conversation resumption after a user closes the app for several days. What is required? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Persisting the conversation turns in the application's own data store
A strategy for reducing the history to fit the window when it grows large
Recording the model and prompt version used so behavior stays consistent
Relying on the API conversation store
Resending the API key with each stored turn

explanation: After days away, the API will not remember anything: it is stateless. The app must persist turns in its own store (A), have a strategy such as truncation, summarization or compaction for when history outgrows the context window (B), and record the model and prompt version so resumed behavior stays consistent and reproducible (C). There is no API-side conversation store to rely on (D) for the Messages API. Resending the API key with stored turns (E) is meaningless and insecure; the key belongs to the server's configuration, not the conversation data.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un equipo debe respaldar la reanudación de la conversación después de que un usuario cierra la aplicación durante varios días. ¿Qué se requiere? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Persistir la conversación gira en el propio almacén de datos de la aplicación.
Una estrategia para reducir el historial para que se ajuste a la ventana cuando crece
Registrar el modelo y la versión del mensaje utilizados para que el comportamiento se mantenga consistente
Confiar en el almacén de conversaciones API
Reenviar la clave API con cada turno almacenado

es.explanation: Administrar el estado de la conversación persistente es una responsabilidad estándar de la aplicación.

question: What is the correct approach when a single document exceeds the model's context window?

options.text: Chunk the document, process chunks independently, then combine or reduce the results
Increase max_tokens to accommodate it
Send it anyway and let the API truncate
Compress the text with Gzip before sending

explanation: When a document exceeds the context window, split it on semantic boundaries (sections, chapters), process chunks independently (a map step, possibly in parallel), and combine or reduce the results (summaries, extractions, or a final synthesis call). Raising max_tokens (B) only limits output length, not input capacity. Sending it anyway (C) results in a validation error; modern API requests exceeding the window are rejected rather than silently truncated. Gzip (D) is irrelevant because the model consumes tokens of text, not bytes, and compressed binary data would not be readable.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es el enfoque correcto cuando un solo documento excede la ventana de contexto del modelo?

options.text: Divida el documento, procese fragmentos de forma independiente y luego combine o reduzca los resultados
Incrementar max_tokens para acomodarlo
Envíalo de todos modos y deja que la API se trunque
Comprime el texto con Gzip antes de enviar

es.explanation: Segmentar los límites semánticos y resumir es el camino correcto para el manejo de contextos prolongados.

question: Which is the most robust way to detect that a response was truncated?

options.text: Check whether stop_reason equals max_tokens
Check whether the last character is a full stop
Attempt to parse the output and treat a failure as truncation
Compare the output length to max_tokens

explanation: The API reports why generation ended in stop_reason; the value max_tokens means the output was cut at the limit, which is the reliable, explicit signal. The last character being a full stop (B) is a heuristic that fails with lists, code or JSON. Parse failure (C) can happen for many reasons other than truncation and is only a secondary check. Comparing output length to max_tokens (D) is fragile because you would need exact token counts, while the API already tells you.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la forma más sólida de detectar que una respuesta fue truncada?

options.text: Compruebe si stop_reason es igual a max_tokens
Compruebe si el último carácter es un punto
Intente analizar el resultado y trate un error como truncamiento
Compare la longitud de salida con max_tokens

es.explanation: La API proporciona explícitamente un campo stop_reason para indicar por qué se detuvo la generación.

question: Which configuration values should be externalized rather than hardcoded in a Claude application? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Model identifier
max_tokens and temperature
Prompt templates
The API key
The JSON parsing logic for tool results

explanation: Operational configuration should live outside the code so it can change without a deploy: the model identifier (A) since models are updated and deprecated, generation parameters such as max_tokens and temperature (B), prompt templates (C) so prompts can be versioned and tuned, and the API key (D), which is a secret and must come from environment variables or a secrets manager. The JSON parsing logic for tool results (E) is application logic tied to the code and its tests; externalizing it adds risk without operational benefit.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué valores de configuración deberían externalizarse en lugar de codificarse en una aplicación Claude? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Identificador de modelo
max_tokens y temperatura
Plantillas de aviso
La clave API
La lógica de análisis JSON para los resultados de la herramienta

es.explanation: Separe la configuración operativa y los secretos de la lógica empresarial codificada.

question: A developer wants to prevent a runaway cost incident from a bug that loops API calls. Which control is most effective?

options.text: Server-side spend limits plus per-request and per-session token budgets enforced in the calling service
Instructing a model to be economical
Setting temperature to zero
Reviewing the bill monthly

explanation: A runaway loop is a systems bug, so controls must be deterministic and outside the model: spend limits configured on the account or workspace, plus per-request and per-session token and iteration budgets enforced by the calling service that abort when exceeded. Asking the model to be economical (B) cannot stop a bug in your loop code. Temperature zero (C) changes sampling, not how many calls are made. Reviewing the bill monthly (D) is detection after the damage is done.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un desarrollador quiere evitar un incidente de costos desbocados debido a un error que repite las llamadas API. ¿Qué control es más eficaz?

options.text: Límites de gasto del lado del servidor más presupuestos de tokens por solicitud y por sesión aplicados en el servicio de llamadas
Instruir a un modelo para que sea económico
Poner la temperatura a cero
Revisar la factura mensualmente

es.explanation: Los controles presupuestarios dentro de la aplicación son la primera línea de defensa contra el uso descontrolado.

question: Which statement about the messages array and images is correct?

options.text: An image block and a text block can appear in the same user message
Images must be in the system prompt
Only the first message may contain an image
Images must be sent in a separate API call

explanation: A user message's content is an array of blocks, and image and text blocks (and documents) can be mixed freely, for example an image followed by a question about it. Images do not belong in the system prompt (B); they are supplied as content blocks in user messages. Any user turn may contain images, not only the first (C), subject to the per-request image limits. A separate API call (D) is unnecessary and would lose the shared context the question relies on.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Vision and document processing

es.question: ¿Qué afirmación sobre la matriz de mensajes y las imágenes es correcta?

options.text: Un bloque de imagen y un bloque de texto pueden aparecer en el mismo mensaje de usuario
Las imágenes deben estar en el indicador del sistema.
Sólo el primer mensaje puede contener una imagen.
Las imágenes deben enviarse en una llamada API separada

es.explanation: Los mensajes pueden contener múltiples bloques de contenido de diferentes tipos.

question: Which are legitimate reasons to implement a response cache in your own application layer, separate from prompt caching? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Identical repeated questions can be served without any API call at all
It reduces latency to near-zero for cache hits
It provides deterministic answers for frequently asked questions
It removes the need for API keys
It increases the model's accuracy

explanation: An application-level response cache sits in front of the API. Exact repeated questions can be answered with no API call at all (A), so hits are essentially instant (B) and the answer is deterministic and stable for FAQ-style traffic (C), which also saves tokens. This is different from prompt caching, which only discounts the prefix but still calls the model. A response cache does not remove the need for API keys (D), because misses still call Claude, and it does not improve accuracy (E); it simply replays prior answers, which could be wrong or stale.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Prompt caching

es.question: ¿Cuáles son razones legítimas para implementar un caché de respuesta en su propia capa de aplicación, aparte del almacenamiento en caché de avisos? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Se pueden atender preguntas repetidas idénticas sin necesidad de realizar ninguna llamada a la API.
Reduce la latencia a casi cero para los accesos al caché
Proporciona respuestas deterministas a preguntas frecuentes.
Elimina la necesidad de claves API
Aumenta la precisión del modelo.

es.explanation: El almacenamiento en caché a nivel de aplicación evita por completo las llamadas API para solicitudes comunes.

question: What is the appropriate response to an API error of type authentication_error?

options.text: Verify and rotate the API key; do not retry with the same credential
Retry with exponential backoff
Reduce max_tokens and retry
Switch to a smaller model

explanation: authentication_error (HTTP 401) means the API key is missing, invalid or revoked. The request will fail identically until credentials are fixed, so the right response is to verify or rotate the key and not retry with the same one. Exponential backoff (B) is for transient errors (429, 5xx, overloaded), not permanent client errors. Lowering max_tokens (C) and switching to a smaller model (D) have no relationship to who you are authenticated as.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la respuesta adecuada a un error de API de tipo autenticación_error?

options.text: Verificar y rotar la clave API; no reintentar con la misma credencial
Reintentar con retroceso exponencial
Reduzca max_tokens y vuelva a intentarlo
Cambiar a un modelo más pequeño

es.explanation: Los errores de autenticación persistirán hasta que se solucionen las credenciales.

question: A service needs to enforce that no single tenant consumes more than a fixed share of capacity. Where should this be implemented?

options.text: In the Claude system prompt
In the application's request pipeline, tracking per-tenant usage and rejecting/queuing over-quota requests
By giving each tenant the API key
By relying on the provider's organization-level rate limits

explanation: Fair sharing among tenants is a business rule that only your application knows about. The request pipeline should track per-tenant usage and reject, queue or throttle over-quota requests. The system prompt (A) cannot enforce capacity because the model has no view of other tenants' usage. Giving each tenant a key (C) spreads secrets, complicates billing and does not itself enforce fair shares. Organization-level rate limits (D) are applied to your whole organization or workspace, not per tenant, so one tenant can still consume the whole quota.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un servicio debe exigir que ningún inquilino consuma más de una parte fija de capacidad. ¿Dónde debería implementarse esto?

options.text: En el mensaje del sistema Claude
En la canalización de solicitudes de la aplicación, realizar un seguimiento del uso por inquilino y rechazar o poner en cola solicitudes que excedan la cuota.
Al darle a cada inquilino la clave API
Confiando en los límites de tarifas a nivel de organización del proveedor

es.explanation: La equidad a nivel de inquilino es una responsabilidad de la capa de aplicación.

question: Which best describes the role of the request_id returned with an API response?

options.text: A unique identifier for the request, useful for correlating logs and support investigations
A token that authenticates subsequent requests
A handle for retrieving the conversation later
An idempotency key that prevents duplicate processing

explanation: Each response carries a request-id (header and request_id field) that uniquely identifies that request. You should log it and quote it to Anthropic support to trace the exact call. It is not a credential (B), cannot be used to retrieve a conversation later (C) because the API is stateless, and it is not an idempotency key (D); the Messages API does not deduplicate requests, so retries can be processed twice.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál describe mejor la función del request_id devuelto con una respuesta API?

options.text: Un identificador único para la solicitud, útil para correlacionar registros e investigaciones de soporte.
Un token que autentica solicitudes posteriores.
Un identificador para recuperar la conversación más tarde.
Una clave de idempotencia que evita el procesamiento duplicado

es.explanation: Es esencial para la depuración y las interacciones de soporte.

question: Which are valid reasons to wrap the Claude SDK in an internal client library? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Consistent retry, timeout, and error classification behavior across services
Uniform structured logging of usage, stop reasons, and prompt versions
A single place to switch models or roll out configuration changes
Hiding the API entirely so developers cannot see request payloads
Enforcing organization-wide guardrails such as PII reduction before sending

explanation: A thin internal wrapper centralizes cross-cutting concerns: consistent retries, timeouts and error classification (A), structured logging of usage, stop reasons and prompt versions (B), a single place to change models or roll out config (C), and organization-wide guardrails such as PII redaction before data leaves (E). Hiding request payloads so developers cannot see them (D) is not a valid goal; it hurts debuggability and transparency and is an anti-pattern.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son razones válidas para empaquetar el SDK de Claude en una biblioteca de cliente interna? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Comportamiento consistente de reintentos, tiempos de espera y clasificación de errores en todos los servicios
Registro estructurado uniforme de uso, motivos de detención y versiones de avisos
Un único lugar para cambiar de modelo o implementar cambios de configuración
Ocultar la API por completo para que los desarrolladores no puedan ver las cargas útiles de las solicitudes
Hacer cumplir las barreras de seguridad en toda la organización, como la reducción de la PII antes del envío

es.explanation: Los contenedores ayudan a estandarizar las preocupaciones transversales en toda su infraestructura.

question: What is the consequence of omitting max_tokens from a Messages API request?

options.text: The request fails validation because max_tokens is required
The model generates until it decides to stop with no cap
The API applies a default of 4096
The response is truncated to one token

explanation: max_tokens is a required parameter of the Messages API, so omitting it fails validation with an invalid_request_error. There is no unlimited generation (B) and no silent default of 4096 (C); the API forces each caller to set an explicit cap, which also bounds cost and latency. The response is never truncated to a single token (D); that would only occur if you set max_tokens to 1.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la consecuencia de omitir max_tokens de una solicitud de API de mensajes?

options.text: La solicitud no supera la validación porque se requiere max_tokens
El modelo genera hasta que decide detenerse sin límite.
La API aplica un valor predeterminado de 4096
La respuesta se trunca a un token.

es.explanation: La API impone una longitud máxima explícita para cada turno.

question: Which describes the correct precedence when Claude code settings conflict across scopes?

options.text: Enterprise-managed settings take precedence over project settings, which take precedence over user settings
User settings always win because they are more specific to the person
The most recently modified file wins
The claude.md overwrites all settings files

explanation: Claude Code applies settings by precedence: enterprise managed policy settings are highest and cannot be overridden, followed by command-line arguments, then local project settings, then shared project settings, then user settings. This lets organizations enforce security policy while developers keep flexibility where not restricted. User settings do not always win (B); they are the lowest. File modification time (C) is irrelevant. CLAUDE.md (D) provides instructions and memory for the model, not configuration, and it cannot override settings files or permissions.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe la precedencia correcta cuando la configuración del código Claude entra en conflicto entre ámbitos?

options.text: La configuración administrada por la empresa tiene prioridad sobre la configuración del proyecto, que a su vez tiene prioridad sobre la configuración del usuario.
La configuración de usuario siempre gana porque es más específica de la persona
El archivo modificado más recientemente gana
El claude.md sobrescribe todos los archivos de configuración.

es.explanation: La configuración jerárquica permite la seguridad en toda la empresa y al mismo tiempo permite la flexibilidad de los desarrolladores locales.

question: Which tasks are well-suited to Claude Code as opposed to a direct API integration? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Multi-file refactoring in an existing repository
Exploring an unfamiliar codebase and explaining how a subsystem works
Serving production chat traffic to end users
Running repetitive repository maintenance via scripted invocations and hooks
Embedding an assistant inside a customer-facing mobile app

explanation: Claude Code is an agentic developer tool that works inside a local repository: multi-file refactors (A), codebase exploration and explanation (B), and scripted maintenance using headless mode and hooks (D) fit well. Serving production chat traffic to end users (C) and embedding an assistant in a customer-facing mobile app (E) are product features that require direct API (or Agent SDK) integration with your own backend, UI, auth and quotas, so Claude Code is the wrong tool.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué tareas se adaptan mejor a Claude Code en comparación con una integración API directa? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Refactorización de múltiples archivos en un repositorio existente
Explorar una base de código desconocida y explicar cómo funciona un subsistema
Sirviendo tráfico de chat de producción a los usuarios finales
Ejecutar mantenimiento repetitivo del repositorio mediante invocaciones y ganchos programados
Integrar un asistente dentro de una aplicación móvil orientada al cliente

es.explanation: Claude Code es una herramienta de desarrollo diseñada para la interacción con repositorios locales.

question: Which practice most improves the debuggability of a multi-turn agent?

options.text: Persisting a complete, structured trace of each turn, including the request payload, tool arguments, tool results, usage, and stop reason
Printing the final answer to the console
Reducing the number of turns allowed
Using a larger model

explanation: Agents are non-deterministic and multi-step, so debugging depends on being able to reconstruct each step. Persist a structured trace per turn with the request payload, tool arguments, tool results, usage and stop reason. Printing only the final answer (B) hides where things went wrong. Reducing the allowed turns (C) limits capability and does not make failures any more visible. A larger model (D) may change error rates but does nothing for observability.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Qué práctica mejora más la capacidad de depuración de un agente de múltiples turnos?

options.text: Mantener un seguimiento completo y estructurado de cada turno, incluida la carga útil de la solicitud, los argumentos de la herramienta, los resultados de la herramienta, el uso y el motivo de la detención.
Imprimiendo la respuesta final a la consola.
Reducir el número de vueltas permitidas
Usando un modelo más grande

es.explanation: Los seguimientos estructurados le permiten ver exactamente qué sucedió en cada paso de la lógica del agente.

question: Which describes the correct use of top_p relative to temperature?

options.text: Adjust one or the other, not both, since they interact in ways that are hard to reason about
Always set both to zero for deterministic output
top_p controls output length
top_p replaces max_tokens

explanation: Temperature and top_p both reshape the sampling distribution, and Anthropic recommends adjusting one, not both, because their interaction is hard to predict (some newer models even reject setting both). Setting both to zero (B) is not a sound recipe: temperature 0 gives near-deterministic output, but results are still not guaranteed identical, and top_p 0 is not meaningful. top_p does not control output length (C); that is max_tokens and stop sequences. It does not replace max_tokens (D), which is still required.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe el uso correcto de top_p en relación con la temperatura?

options.text: Ajuste uno u otro, no ambos, ya que interactúan de maneras sobre las cuales es difícil razonar.
Establezca siempre ambos en cero para una salida determinista
top_p controla la longitud de salida
top_p reemplaza max_tokens

es.explanation: Ajustar ambos crea interacciones complejas que son difíciles de predecir.

question: A workload sends the same 8000-token instruction block with a different user query 50,000 times a day; which combination gives the largest saving? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Prompt caching the instruction block behind a break point
Auditing the instruction block and removing redundant content
Evaluating whether a smaller model meets the quality bar
Increasing max_tokens
Disabling streaming

explanation: With a large identical prefix and 50,000 calls a day, the savings stack: caching the instruction block behind a cache breakpoint (A) makes subsequent reads cost a fraction of base input price, auditing and trimming redundant instructions (B) reduces the tokens that must be sent and cached at all, and testing a smaller model against your eval bar (C) lowers the per-token rate if quality holds. Increasing max_tokens (D) only raises the ceiling on spend and does nothing to reduce cost. Disabling streaming (E) does not change token counts or price.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Una carga de trabajo envía el mismo bloque de instrucciones de 8000 tokens con una consulta de usuario diferente 50 000 veces al día; ¿Qué combinación produce el mayor ahorro? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Solicitar almacenamiento en caché del bloque de instrucciones detrás de un punto de interrupción
Auditar el bloque de instrucciones y eliminar contenido redundante
Evaluar si un modelo más pequeño cumple con el estándar de calidad
Incrementando max_tokens
Deshabilitar la transmisión

es.explanation: Costes de ataque reduciendo el volumen de entrada, almacenando en caché lo que queda y seleccionando el modelo más eficiente.

question: What is the main disadvantage of always enabling extended thinking?

options.text: It increases latency and output token cost even on tasks that gain nothing from it
It disables tool use
It reduces accuracy on hard problems
It prevents streaming

explanation: Extended thinking makes the model spend thinking tokens before answering, and those are billed as output tokens and add latency. For simple tasks that gain nothing, you pay more and wait longer for no benefit, so it should be enabled when problems benefit from deliberate reasoning. It does not disable tool use (B), though there are some constraints with tool_choice. It improves, rather than reduces, accuracy on hard problems (C). It does not prevent streaming (D); thinking is streamed as thinking deltas.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la principal desventaja de permitir siempre el pensamiento extendido?

options.text: Aumenta la latencia y el costo del token de salida incluso en tareas que no obtienen nada de ello.
Inhabilita el uso de herramientas
Reduce la precisión en problemas difíciles.
Impide la transmisión

es.explanation: Utilice el pensamiento extendido únicamente para tareas complejas, ya que agrega costos y latencia.

question: Which describes an appropriate quality bar for choosing a production model?

options.text: The threshold derived from what the product needs to be useful and safe, measured on a representative eval set
100% accuracy on all inputs
Matching the largest available model exactly
Whatever the model achieves out of the box

explanation: A quality bar should be set from product requirements (usefulness, safety, error tolerance) and measured on a representative eval set built from real inputs, so the model choice is evidence-based. 100% accuracy (B) is unrealistic and would make every model fail. Matching the largest model exactly (C) ties the bar to a reference rather than to what the product needs, and wastes cost if a cheaper model suffices. Accepting whatever the model achieves (D) is no bar at all, so you cannot tell if it is good enough.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe una barra de calidad adecuada para elegir un modelo de producción?

options.text: El umbral derivado de lo que el producto necesita para ser útil y seguro, medido en un conjunto de evaluaciones representativo.
100% de precisión en todas las entradas
Coincidiendo exactamente con el modelo más grande disponible
Lo que el modelo logra fuera de la caja

es.explanation: Defina su barra de calidad en función de las necesidades del producto y la tolerancia a errores antes de evaluar los modelos.

question: Which are true statements about latency in LLM applications? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Total latency scales with the number of output tokens generated
Prefill time scales with input length and is reduced by cache hits
Multi-turn agent loops multiply latency by the number of turns
Latency is unaffected by model size
Streaming reduces total generation time

explanation: Total latency grows with the number of output tokens, because generation is sequential (A). Prefill time grows with input length and is lowered by prompt cache hits (B). In an agent loop each turn is a separate model call, so latency multiplies with turn count (C). Larger models are generally slower (D is false). Streaming (E) improves perceived latency, since the first tokens show up sooner, but total generation time stays the same.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son las afirmaciones verdaderas sobre la latencia en las aplicaciones LLM? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: La latencia total aumenta con la cantidad de tokens de salida generados
El tiempo de precarga aumenta con la longitud de la entrada y se reduce con los accesos al caché
Los bucles de agente de varios turnos multiplican la latencia por el número de turnos
La latencia no se ve afectada por el tamaño del modelo.
El streaming reduce el tiempo total de generación

es.explanation: La latencia es acumulativa entre turnos y depende de la longitud total de la secuencia.

question: A team finds that a smaller model matches the larger one on 94% of eval cases but fails on complex multi-step reasoning. What is the best design?

options.text: Use the small model by default and escalate to the large model when a cheap difficulty or confidence signal indicates a hard case
Use the large model for everything
Use the small model for everything and accept the failures
Alternate between models randomly

explanation: This is the routing pattern: a cheap check (a classifier, heuristic, or the small model's own confidence) sends easy cases to the small model and escalates hard multi-step cases to the large model. That keeps most of the cost and latency benefits while fixing the failures. Using the large model for everything (B) pays more when 94% of cases do not need it. Accepting failures (C) ignores a known quality gap on hard cases. Random alternation (D) provides no relationship between difficulty and model, so it gets neither the savings nor the quality.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un equipo descubre que un modelo más pequeño coincide con el más grande en el 94% de los casos de evaluación, pero falla en un razonamiento complejo de varios pasos. ¿Cuál es el mejor diseño?

options.text: Utilice el modelo pequeño de forma predeterminada y escale al modelo grande cuando una dificultad barata o una señal de confianza indique un caso difícil.
Usa el modelo grande para todo
Utiliza el modelo pequeño para todo y acepta los fallos.
Alternar entre modelos aleatoriamente

es.explanation: El enrutamiento a un modelo más grande para casos complejos mantiene tanto el rendimiento como la rentabilidad.

question: Which statement about token counting is most accurate for cost estimation?

options.text: Measure actual token counts from the usage object rather than estimating from characters or words
One token equals four characters universally
One token equals one word
Token counts are the same across all providers

explanation: Token counts vary with the tokenizer, language, code and formatting, so heuristics are only rough. The reliable way to account for cost is to read the usage object returned on each response (input, output, cache read and write tokens) or use the token counting endpoint before sending. One token equals four characters (B) and one token equals one word (C) are rough rules of thumb for English only. Token counts differ between providers and even between Claude model generations (D) because tokenizers differ.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué afirmación sobre el recuento de tokens es más precisa para la estimación de costos?

options.text: Mida el recuento real de tokens a partir del objeto de uso en lugar de realizar estimaciones a partir de caracteres o palabras.
Un token equivale a cuatro caracteres universalmente
Una ficha equivale a una palabra
Los recuentos de tokens son los mismos en todos los proveedores

es.explanation: Utilice siempre el objeto de uso devuelto para una contabilidad precisa.

question: What is the primary cost consideration unique to agentic systems compared with single-call applications?

options.text: Context accumulates across turns and is resent each time, so cost grows superlinearly with turn count
Agents are billed at a higher per-token rate
Tool definitions are billed separately from tokens
Agents require the largest model

explanation: An agent re-sends the conversation, including prior tool calls and results, on every turn, so input tokens accumulate and total cost across N turns grows faster than linearly (roughly quadratic if each turn adds a similar amount). Prompt caching and context trimming mitigate this. Agents are not billed at a higher per-token rate (B); the same model pricing applies. Tool definitions (C) are counted as input tokens, not billed separately. Agents do not necessarily require the largest model (D); many use smaller models for subtasks.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál es la consideración de costo principal exclusiva de los sistemas agentes en comparación con las aplicaciones de llamada única?

options.text: El contexto se acumula a lo largo de los turnos y se resiente cada vez, por lo que el costo crece de manera superlineal con el recuento de turnos.
A los agentes se les factura a una tarifa por token más alta
Las definiciones de herramientas se facturan por separado de los tokens
Los agentes requieren el modelo más grande

es.explanation: El reenvío frecuente de contexto es el generador de costos más importante en los agentes de múltiples turnos.

question: Which describes the correct approach to setting a per-request cost ceiling?

options.text: Cap max_tokens, cap agent iterations, and abort when a cumulative token budget is exceeded
Rely on the model to stop when it has done enough
Set temperature to zero
Check the monthly invoice

explanation: Cost ceilings must be hard limits in the harness: cap max_tokens per call, cap the number of agent iterations, and track cumulative token usage from the usage objects, aborting or escalating once the budget is exceeded. Relying on the model to stop (B) is not a guarantee. Temperature zero (C) does not affect the number of tokens or calls. The monthly invoice (D) only shows the damage after the fact.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál describe el enfoque correcto para establecer un límite de costo por solicitud?

options.text: Limitar max_tokens, limitar las iteraciones del agente y cancelar cuando se excede un presupuesto de token acumulado
Confíe en que el modelo se detendrá cuando haya hecho lo suficiente.
Poner la temperatura a cero
Consulta la factura mensual

es.explanation: Establezca límites estrictos en el arnés para evitar costos descontrolados.

question: Which describes the correct order in which to apply prompt engineering techniques?

options.text: Be clear and direct, add examples, allow reasoning, add structure with tags, assign a role. Then consider prefilling and chaining
Start with chain-of-thought and add clarity only if it fails
Start by chaining prompts into a multi-call workflow
Start by increasing the model size

explanation: Anthropic's prompt engineering guidance runs from the most broadly effective and cheapest techniques to more advanced ones: be clear and direct, use examples (multishot), let the model think (chain of thought), structure with XML tags, give a role, and only then consider prefilling and prompt chaining. Starting from chain-of-thought (B) skips the basics that often fix the problem. Starting with chaining (C) adds complexity, latency and cost before you know it is needed. Increasing model size (D) is a costly last resort compared with improving the prompt.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál describe el orden correcto en el que aplicar técnicas de ingeniería rápidas?

options.text: Sea claro y directo, agregue ejemplos, permita el razonamiento, agregue estructura con etiquetas, asigne un rol. Entonces considere precargar y encadenar
Comience con una cadena de pensamiento y agregue claridad solo si falla
Comience encadenando indicaciones en un flujo de trabajo de múltiples llamadas
Comience aumentando el tamaño del modelo.

es.explanation: Comience de manera simple y agregue complejidad solo cuando sea necesario.

question: An agent's context contains the full text of 12 web pages it fetched. Which techniques reclaim context without losing the ability to answer? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Replace full page text with per-page extractive summaries relevant to the goal
Store full pages externally and keep only identifiers and summaries in context
Drop pages that the agent has already determined to be irrelevant
Keep everything in case it becomes relevant later
Convert the pages to a single unlabeled concatenated block

explanation: Context is a limited resource. Replacing full pages with goal-relevant extractive summaries (A) keeps the facts needed and drops bulk. Storing full pages externally and keeping identifiers plus summaries in context (B) lets the agent re-fetch details on demand (just-in-time retrieval). Dropping pages already judged irrelevant (C) removes pure noise. Keeping everything (D) is exactly the problem, since it saturates context and degrades focus. Merging pages into one unlabeled block (E) does not reduce tokens and removes the source structure the agent needs.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: El contexto de un agente contiene el texto completo de 12 páginas web que obtuvo. ¿Qué técnicas recuperan el contexto sin perder la capacidad de respuesta? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Reemplace el texto de la página completa con resúmenes extractivos por página relevantes para el objetivo
Almacene páginas completas externamente y mantenga solo identificadores y resúmenes en contexto
Eliminar páginas que el agente ya haya determinado que son irrelevantes
Guarda todo por si se vuelve relevante más adelante
Convierta las páginas en un único bloque concatenado sin etiquetar

es.explanation: Gestionar el contexto como un recurso limitado; almacene la mayor parte externamente e indexe con resúmenes.

question: What is the most likely effect of a system prompt that is 15,000 tokens of loosely organized rules?

options.text: Higher cost per request, slower prefill, and inconsistent instruction adherence
Better accuracy because more guidance is always better
No effect since system prompts are free
The model will ignore the system prompt entirely

explanation: A very long, loosely organized system prompt costs more for every request (unless cached), adds prefill latency, and dilutes the model's attention, so rules conflict or get missed and adherence becomes inconsistent. More guidance is not always better (B); clear, organized and prioritized instructions are. System prompts are not free (C); they are billed as input tokens. The model does not ignore them wholesale (D), it follows them unevenly.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Prompt engineering best practices

es.question: ¿Cuál es el efecto más probable de un aviso del sistema que consta de 15.000 tokens de reglas poco organizadas?

options.text: Mayor costo por solicitud, llenado previo más lento y cumplimiento inconsistente de las instrucciones
Mayor precisión porque más orientación siempre es mejor
Sin efecto ya que las indicaciones del sistema son gratuitas
El modelo ignorará por completo el mensaje del sistema.

es.explanation: Las indicaciones largas y desorganizadas aumentan la latencia previa al llenado y disminuyen la calidad de la instrucción.

question: Which technique best prevents a model from confusing user-supplied data with instructions?

options.text: Enclosing the data in clearly named tags and stating that content inside is data to be processed, not instructions to follow
Placing the data at the end without any delimiter
Lowering the temperature
Putting the data in the system prompt

explanation: To prevent prompt-injection-style confusion, wrap untrusted data in clearly named tags (for example <document>) and state in the instructions that the content within is data to process and not instructions to follow. Delimiters give the model a structural boundary, though this reduces rather than eliminates risk and should be combined with other controls. Placing data at the end without delimiters (B) blurs where instructions end. Lowering temperature (C) does not alter what the model treats as instruction. Putting data in the system prompt (D) gives it higher authority, which is the opposite of what is wanted for untrusted content.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué técnica evita mejor que un modelo confunda los datos proporcionados por el usuario con instrucciones?

options.text: Incluir los datos en etiquetas con nombres claros e indicar que el contenido que contiene son datos que se procesarán, no instrucciones a seguir.
Colocando los datos al final sin ningún delimitador
Bajando la temperatura
Poner los datos en el indicador del sistema.

es.explanation: Los delimitadores estructurales claros ayudan al modelo a distinguir entre instrucciones y datos de entrada.

question: Why is it useful to ask the model to state when it cannot answer from the provided context?

options.text: It gives the model an acceptable alternative to fabricating, reducing hallucination
It reduces token cost
It disables the model's general knowledge
It is required by the API

explanation: Models tend to produce plausible answers when asked a question. Explicitly permitting a response such as 'the context does not contain this information' gives an acceptable alternative to fabricating, which lowers hallucination in grounded Q&A. It does not directly reduce token cost (B). It does not disable general knowledge (C); that would require an explicit instruction to use only the provided context. It is not an API requirement (D); it is a prompting practice.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Por qué es útil pedirle al modelo que indique cuándo no puede responder desde el contexto proporcionado?

options.text: Le da al modelo una alternativa aceptable a la fabricación, reduciendo las alucinaciones.
Reduce el costo del token
Desactiva el conocimiento general del modelo.
Es requerido por la API

es.explanation: Darle una "salida" al modelo reduce la probabilidad de que invente hechos.

question: Which are effective ways to structure a prompt that must handle several distinct input types? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Tag each input section with a descriptive name and reference those names in the instructions
Provide an example for each input type showing the expected handling
State explicitly what to do when an expected section is missing
Merge all inputs into one block so the model decides what is what
Use inconsistent tag names to encourage flexible interpretation

explanation: Multi-input prompts work best when each input is tagged with a descriptive name and the instructions refer to those names (A), when there is an example showing expected handling per input type (B), and when the prompt says what to do if a section is missing or empty (C), avoiding guessing. Merging everything into one block (D) forces the model to infer boundaries and invites errors. Inconsistent tag names (E) create ambiguity; Anthropic recommends consistent, meaningful tag names.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son formas efectivas de estructurar un mensaje que debe manejar varios tipos de entrada distintos? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Etiquete cada sección de entrada con un nombre descriptivo y haga referencia a esos nombres en las instrucciones.
Proporcione un ejemplo para cada tipo de entrada que muestre el manejo esperado.
Indique explícitamente qué hacer cuando falta una sección esperada
Fusionar todas las entradas en un bloque para que el modelo decida qué es qué
Utilice nombres de etiquetas inconsistentes para fomentar una interpretación flexible

es.explanation: La claridad estructural y los ejemplos explícitos mejoran significativamente la precisión de las entradas de varias partes.

question: Which describes the correct threat model for tool arguments generated by a model?

options.text: Treat them as untrusted user input subject to full validation, allow-listing, and escaping
Trust them because the model generated them from your own prompt
Validate only the types since the schema guarantees safety
Validate only when the agent is user-facing

explanation: Tool arguments are generated by a model that can be influenced by user input or by injected content in retrieved data, so they are effectively untrusted input. Treat them like any request parameter: validate against the schema and business rules, allow-list values (paths, commands, hosts), and escape before using in SQL, shell or file operations. Trusting them (B) ignores prompt injection risks. A schema (C) only guarantees shape, not safety (a valid string can still be a malicious path or query). Validating only for user-facing agents (D) is wrong because injection can arrive through tool results and documents even without a direct user.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál describe el modelo de amenaza correcto para los argumentos de herramienta generados por un modelo?

options.text: Trátelos como entradas de usuarios que no son de confianza y están sujetos a validación completa, listas de permitidos y escape.
Confíe en ellos porque el modelo los generó a partir de su propio mensaje.
Validar solo los tipos ya que el esquema garantiza la seguridad.
Validar solo cuando el agente esté de cara al usuario

es.explanation: Los argumentos de herramientas generados por el modelo siempre deben tratarse como entradas que no son de confianza.

question: Which measures reduce the risk of sensitive data leaking through an LLM feature? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Redacting or tokenizing PII before it is sent to the model
Applying access controls so the retrieval layer only returns documents the requesting user may see
Filtering outputs for sensitive patterns before display
Storing full prompts and completions indefinitely for debugging
Setting retention limits and access controls on request logs

explanation: Data leak risk is reduced in layers: redact or tokenize PII before sending (A), enforce access control in retrieval so the user only gets documents they may see (B), filter outputs for sensitive patterns such as keys or identifiers before display (C), and set retention limits and access controls on logs (E). Storing prompts and completions indefinitely (D) expands the exposure surface and is the opposite of data minimization. Note: option C originally read 'non-sensitive patterns', which was a typo and has been corrected to 'sensitive patterns'; the key remains A, B, C and E.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué medidas reducen el riesgo de que se filtren datos confidenciales a través de una función LLM? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Redactar o tokenizar la PII antes de enviarla al modelo
Aplicar controles de acceso para que la capa de recuperación solo devuelva documentos que el usuario solicitante pueda ver
Filtrado de salidas para patrones no sensibles antes de mostrarlos
Almacenamiento de indicaciones y finalizaciones completas de forma indefinida para depuración
Establecer límites de retención y controles de acceso en registros de solicitudes

es.explanation: La defensa en profundidad, desde el filtrado de recuperación hasta la retención de registros, minimiza los riesgos de exposición de datos.

question: What is the correct security posture for an agent that can execute code?

options.text: Run it in an isolated sandbox with no network access, restricted file system scope, resource limits, and no production credentials
Run it as the application user with normal privileges
Rely on the model refusing to write harmful code
Review the code manually after execution

explanation: Code-executing agents can run harmful or buggy code, whether from prompt injection or from model error, so security must come from the environment, not from the model's behavior: an isolated sandbox with no network (or tightly allow-listed), restricted file system scope, CPU/memory/time limits, and no production credentials. Running with normal application privileges (B) gives a compromised agent everything the app can do. Relying on the model to refuse (C) is not a security control, as it can be bypassed. Manual review after execution (D) is too late because the damage has already occurred.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál es la postura de seguridad correcta para un agente que puede ejecutar código?

options.text: Ejecútelo en un entorno aislado sin acceso a la red, alcance restringido del sistema de archivos, límites de recursos y sin credenciales de producción.
Ejecútelo como usuario de la aplicación con privilegios normales.
Confíe en que el modelo se niegue a escribir código dañino
Revisar el código manualmente después de la ejecución.

es.explanation: La ejecución de código es de alto riesgo; utilice un entorno de pruebas estrictamente para evitar el impacto en el sistema.

question: Which is the best description of defense in depth for an agentic application?

options.text: Multiple independent controls at different layers so that failure of any one does not result in harm
Using the largest available model
Writing a very detailed system prompt
Logging everything

explanation: Defense in depth means stacking independent controls at different layers, such as input validation, least-privilege tools, sandboxing, output filtering, human approval for risky actions, and monitoring, so that a failure of one layer does not cause harm. A larger model (B) is not a control and can still be manipulated. A detailed system prompt (C) is one soft layer that can be overridden by injection. Logging everything (D) helps detection and audit but does not prevent harm by itself.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál es la mejor descripción de defensa en profundidad para una aplicación agente?

options.text: Múltiples controles independientes en diferentes capas para que el fallo de cualquiera de ellos no provoque daños
Usando el modelo más grande disponible
Escribir un mensaje del sistema muy detallado
Registrando todo

es.explanation: La defensa en profundidad supone que los componentes individuales pueden fallar y proporciona capas de protección.

question: Which are appropriate design rules for tool input schemas? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Use descriptive parameter names with clear descriptions and explicit formats or units
Constrain values with enums where the valid set is known
Mark genuinely required fields as required and give sensible defaults elsewhere
Accept a single free-text blob and parse it inside the tool
Keep the parameter count as small as the task genuinely allows

explanation: Good tool schemas help the model fill inputs correctly: descriptive names with clear descriptions and explicit formats or units (A), enums where the valid set is known (B), required only for truly required fields and sensible defaults elsewhere (C), and as few parameters as the task needs (E) to reduce errors and tokens. A single free-text blob parsed inside the tool (D) pushes structure back onto fragile string parsing and removes the schema's validation and guidance for the model.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son las reglas de diseño apropiadas para los esquemas de entrada de herramientas? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Utilice nombres de parámetros descriptivos con descripciones claras y formatos o unidades explícitos.
Restringir valores con enumeraciones donde se conoce el conjunto válido
Marque los campos realmente obligatorios como obligatorios y proporcione valores predeterminados sensatos en otros lugares
Acepte un único blob de texto libre y analícelo dentro de la herramienta
Mantenga el recuento de parámetros tan pequeño como la tarea realmente lo permita.

es.explanation: Los esquemas bien definidos permiten que el modelo proporcione entradas correctas de manera confiable.

question: An MCP server exposes a prompt primitive; who typically triggers it?

options.text: The user through the host application's interface, such as a slash command
The model autonomously during reasoning
The server on a schedule
The Anthropic API

explanation: In MCP, prompts are user-controlled primitives: reusable templates the server exposes and the user selects through the host UI, typically as slash commands or menu entries. Tools are the model-controlled primitive (the model decides to call them), and resources are application-controlled. So the model does not trigger prompts autonomously (B), the server does not fire them on a schedule (C), and the Anthropic API (D) has no role in invoking them.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

es.question: Un servidor MCP expone una primitiva de aviso; ¿Quién suele desencadenarlo?

options.text: El usuario a través de la interfaz de la aplicación host, como un comando de barra diagonal
El modelo de forma autónoma durante el razonamiento.
El servidor en un horario
La API antrópica

es.explanation: Las indicaciones en MCP son generalmente primitivas iniciadas por el usuario.

question: What is the risk of connecting an untrusted third-party MCP server to an agent with broad permissions?

options.text: The server can expose tools and content that manipulate the agent into harmful actions and may exfiltrate data passed to it
The server will slow down the model
The server changes the model's weights
There is no risk because MCP is a standard

explanation: MCP servers supply tool descriptions, results and content that enter the model's context, so a malicious or compromised server can inject instructions (tool poisoning, prompt injection) that steer an agent with broad permissions into harmful actions, and it also receives whatever data the agent passes in, enabling exfiltration. Only trusted servers should be connected, with least-privilege and approval for sensitive actions. Slowing the model (B) is not the main risk. MCP servers cannot change model weights (C). MCP being a standard (D) means interoperability, not safety.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

es.question: ¿Cuál es el riesgo de conectar un servidor MCP de terceros que no es de confianza a un agente con permisos amplios?

options.text: El servidor puede exponer herramientas y contenido que manipulan al agente para realizar acciones dañinas y pueden filtrar datos que se le pasan.
El servidor ralentizará el modelo.
El servidor cambia los pesos del modelo.
No hay riesgo porque MCP es un estándar

es.explanation: Los servidores MCP son integraciones; si no son de confianza, pueden comprometer al agente.

question: Which is the correct way to handle a tool that can return very large results?

options.text: Paginate or truncate with a continuation handle and return a summary plus a reference to the full data
Return everything so the model has full information
Return nothing and let the model ask again
Compress the result with Base64

explanation: Large tool results fill the context, raise cost and latency and hurt focus. Better is to paginate or truncate, return a summary plus a reference or continuation token so the model can request more only when needed. Returning everything (B) saturates context. Returning nothing (C) leaves the model with no useful information and causes needless loops. Base64 (D) actually inflates the size by about a third and adds no semantic compression.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la forma correcta de manejar una herramienta que puede arrojar resultados muy grandes?

options.text: Paginar o truncar con un identificador de continuación y devolver un resumen más una referencia a los datos completos
Devuelve todo para que el modelo tenga la información completa.
No devuelvas nada y deja que el modelo vuelva a preguntar.
Comprimir el resultado con Base64

es.explanation: Evite la saturación del contexto proporcionando resúmenes y paginación para grandes conjuntos de datos.

question: Which statements about the client-server relationship in MCP are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A host application can connect to multiple MCP servers simultaneously
The client mediates between the host and a server, handling the protocol exchange
Servers can be local processes or remote services
Servers connect directly to the language model
A server must implement all three primitives

explanation: MCP uses a host-client-server architecture. A host application (e.g., Claude Desktop or Claude Code) can run several clients and thus connect to multiple servers at once (A). Each client keeps a one-to-one connection with a server and mediates protocol exchange between host and server (B). Servers can be local processes over stdio or remote services over HTTP (C). Servers do not connect directly to the model (D); the host mediates, and the model sees only what the host passes in. A server need not implement all three primitives (E); it can expose any subset of tools, resources and prompts.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

es.question: ¿Qué afirmaciones sobre la relación cliente-servidor en MCP son correctas? (Seleccione todo lo que corresponda)

options.text: Una aplicación host puede conectarse a varios servidores MCP simultáneamente
El cliente media entre el host y un servidor, manejando el intercambio de protocolos.
Los servidores pueden ser procesos locales o servicios remotos.
Los servidores se conectan directamente al modelo de lenguaje.
Un servidor debe implementar las tres primitivas.

es.explanation: La arquitectura MCP utiliza un modelo host-cliente-servidor para facilitar la comunicación.

question: An agent's average task now takes 40 turns, up from 12 after a new tool was added that returns full HTML pages. Task success has dropped. What is the most likely causal chain?

options.text: The larger tool set confused model selection so turns increased
Verbose tool results filled the context degrading the agent's reasoning so it took more turns and still failed more often
The model version changed
Rate limiting slowed the agent down

explanation: Option B is the causal chain: a tool that returns full HTML pages floods the context with markup, navigation and scripts, which dilutes the signal, degrades the model's reasoning over later turns, and forces extra turns to re-find information, so turns rise and success falls together. The fix is to extract and trim at the tool boundary (convert HTML to relevant text, strip boilerplate, cap length). A is wrong because one added tool does not explain a jump from 12 to 40 turns paired with worse success; the symptom points at result size, not the number of tools. C is wrong because nothing in the scenario indicates a model change, and a change tied exactly to the new tool is the stronger signal. D is wrong because rate limiting adds latency or 429 errors but does not increase the number of turns or lower task success. Track turns per task and tokens per turn as leading indicators of context health.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: La tarea promedio de un agente ahora toma 40 turnos, en comparación con 12 después de que se agregó una nueva herramienta que devuelve páginas HTML completas. El éxito de la tarea ha disminuido. ¿Cuál es la cadena causal más probable?

options.text: El conjunto de herramientas más grande confundió la selección del modelo, por lo que los turnos aumentaron
Los resultados detallados de la herramienta llenaron el contexto y degradaron el razonamiento del agente, por lo que tomó más turnos y aun así falló con más frecuencia.
La versión del modelo cambió.
La limitación de velocidad ralentizó al agente

es.explanation: Extraiga y recorte en el límite de la herramienta. Convierta HTML a texto relevante, elimine la navegación y los scripts, y limite la longitud. Mida los turnos por tarea y los tokens por turno como indicadores principales del estado del contexto.

question: A workflow uses a cheap model to classify a ticket then routes to a specialized handler. Classification accuracy is 88%. What is the most important consequence?

options.text: Roughly one in eight tickets reaches the wrong handler so handlers need a way to detect and reroute misclassifications
The system will be 88% cheaper
The classifier should be removed
The handlers should all use the same prompt

explanation: At 88% accuracy roughly 12% (about one in eight) of tickets reach a handler built for something else, so the design must assume misroutes happen. Handlers should have an explicit 'this does not belong to me' output that re-enters routing, and those events should be logged to improve the classifier.
