B is wrong because accuracy says nothing about cost; the saving comes from using a cheap model, not from the accuracy figure. C is wrong because routing with a cheap classifier is the standard pattern from Building effective agents and 88% is improvable (better prompt, examples, evals). D is wrong because the point of routing is to let each handler have a specialized prompt; forcing one prompt discards that benefit and does not fix misclassification.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un flujo de trabajo utiliza un modelo económico para clasificar un ticket y luego lo dirige a un controlador especializado. La precisión de la clasificación es del 88%. ¿Cuál es la consecuencia más importante?

options.text: Aproximadamente uno de cada ocho tickets llega al gestor equivocado, por lo que los gestores necesitan una forma de detectar y redirigir las clasificaciones erróneas.
El sistema será un 88% más barato
El clasificador debe ser eliminado.
Todos los manejadores deben usar el mismo mensaje.

es.explanation: En los flujos de trabajo de enrutamiento, mida la precisión de la clasificación por separado de la calidad del controlador. Proporcione a cada controlador una salida explícita de "esto no me pertenece" que vuelva a ingresar al enrutamiento y registre esos eventos para mejorar el clasificador.

question: Which conditions must hold for an agent to reliably self-correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: The environment returns ground truth feedback the agent can interpret
Errors are surfaced as informative structured signals rather than silent failures
The agent has an action available that can actually address the failure
The temperature is set high enough to try random alternatives
The agent has unlimited turns

explanation: Self-correction is a property of the harness as much as the model. A is needed because the agent must observe ground truth (test output, compiler errors, API responses) to know it failed. B is needed because silent failures or vague errors give nothing to correct from, while structured, informative errors tell the agent what went wrong. C is needed because even a perfectly diagnosed failure cannot be fixed if no available action can address it. D is wrong because randomness from high temperature does not create information and makes behavior less reliable; correction should be driven by feedback, not by random retries. E is wrong because unlimited turns do not enable correction and are actually unsafe; Anthropic recommends stopping conditions or a maximum iteration count to keep control. Where feedback is weak, prefer a workflow with deterministic validation between steps.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Qué condiciones deben cumplirse para que un agente se autocorrija de manera confiable? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: El entorno devuelve información real sobre el terreno que el agente puede interpretar.
Los errores surgen como señales informativas estructuradas en lugar de fallas silenciosas.
El agente tiene una acción disponible que realmente puede abordar la falla.
La temperatura se establece lo suficientemente alta como para probar alternativas aleatorias.
El agente tiene turnos ilimitados.

es.explanation: La autocorrección depende más del arnés que del modelo. Una buena retroalimentación, errores informativos y herramientas de remediación adecuadas son clave; donde la retroalimentación es débil, prefiera un flujo de trabajo con validación determinista entre pasos.

question: A developer is deciding whether to give an agent one broad 'query_database' tool with a free-form SQL parameter or several narrow tools. Which factor most favors the narrow tools?

options.text: Narrow tools produce fewer output tokens
Narrow tools bound what the agent can do making authorization, validation, and auditing trackable
Narrow tools require no descriptions
Narrow tools are cached automatically

explanation: B is correct because narrow, parameterized tools define exactly which actions are possible, so you can authorize, validate inputs, rate limit and audit each one in code. A free-form SQL parameter pushes the security boundary into the model, and a model's judgment is not a security boundary (prompt injection or a mistake could issue destructive or cross-tenant queries). The cost is less flexibility and more tools to describe. A is wrong because the number of output tokens depends on result size and verbosity, not tool granularity. C is wrong because every tool needs a clear description; Anthropic stresses that detailed descriptions are the most important factor in tool performance. D is wrong because caching is something you enable with cache_control on a prefix, and is not automatic or related to tool breadth.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un desarrollador está decidiendo si le dará a un agente una herramienta amplia de 'query_database' con un parámetro SQL de formato libre o varias herramientas limitadas. ¿Qué factor favorece más las herramientas estrechas?

options.text: Las herramientas estrechas producen menos tokens de salida
Herramientas limitadas que limitan lo que el agente puede hacer, haciendo que la autorización, la validación y la auditoría sean rastreables.
Las herramientas estrechas no requieren descripciones
Las herramientas limitadas se almacenan en caché automáticamente

es.explanation: Los parámetros de consulta de formato libre introducen el límite de seguridad en el modelo, que no puede ser un límite de seguridad. Las herramientas estrechas y parametrizadas mantienen la validación en el código que corresponde, a costa de cierta flexibilidad.

question: Which describes the appropriate use of a verification step in an agentic pipeline?

options.text: Deterministic or model-based check that the produced artifact satisfies stated criteria before it is delivered or acted upon
Asking the model whether it is confident
Rerunning the same prompt and comparing outputs for identity
Logging the output for later human review

explanation: A is correct: a verification step checks that the produced artifact meets stated criteria before it is delivered or acted upon, which is the evaluator or gate pattern in Building effective agents. Prefer deterministic checks wherever the property is checkable in code (schema validation, compilation, tests, arithmetic), and use model-based grading with a rubric only for subjective criteria. B is wrong because a model's self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated and is not evidence about the artifact. C is wrong because identical outputs only show consistency, and a model can be consistently wrong; also non-identical but correct outputs would be flagged. D is wrong because logging for later review is observability, not verification: the bad output has already been acted on.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál describe el uso apropiado de un paso de verificación en una canalización agente?

options.text: Verificación determinista o basada en modelos de que el artefacto producido satisface los criterios establecidos antes de ser entregado o de que se actúe sobre él.
Preguntar al modelo si tiene confianza.
Volver a ejecutar el mismo mensaje y comparar resultados para la identidad
Registrar el resultado para su posterior revisión humana

es.explanation: Prefiera la verificación determinista siempre que la propiedad se pueda verificar en el código (esquema, compilación, pruebas, aprobación de aritmética). Utilice la calificación basada en modelos sólo para criterios genuinamente subjetivos con una rúbrica.

question: An orchestrator dispatches 8 parallel workers that fail with tool errors. What should the orchestrator do?

options.text: Abort the whole task
Retry the failed subtasks with backoff and if they still fail, synthesize from the successful results while explicitly flagging the gaps
Silently omit the failed subtasks from the synthesis
Substitute the orchestrator's own guess for the failed subtasks

explanation: B is correct: fan-out needs an explicit partial-failure policy. Retrying with backoff handles transient tool errors; if some subtasks still fail, the orchestrator should synthesize from what succeeded and clearly disclose what is missing, so the consumer can judge the result. A is wrong because discarding seven or so successful results over some failures wastes work, though a threshold below which the whole task fails is a legitimate part of the policy. C is wrong because silently omitting failures produces a confident but incomplete answer the reader cannot detect. D is wrong because the orchestrator substituting its own guess fabricates data presented as worker results, which is hallucination hidden inside a pipeline.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un orquestador envía 8 trabajadores paralelos que fallan con errores de herramienta. ¿Qué debe hacer el orquestador?

options.text: Cancelar toda la tarea
Vuelva a intentar las subtareas fallidas con retroceso y, si aún fallan, sintetice a partir de los resultados exitosos mientras marca explícitamente las brechas.
Omitir silenciosamente las subtareas fallidas de la síntesis.
Sustituir las subtareas fallidas por las propias suposiciones del orquestador

es.explanation: Los patrones de dispersión necesitan una política explícita de falla parcial: presupuesto de reintento por trabajador, un umbral por debajo del cual falla toda la tarea y divulgación obligatoria de lo que no se pudo completar.

question: Which are reasonable metrics to monitor for a production agent? Select all that apply.

options.text: Turns per completed task
Tokens and cost per completed task
Tool error rate by tool
Rate of hitting the maximum iteration cap
Average length of the system prompt

explanation: A, B, C and D are outcome and reliability signals. Turns per task and tokens/cost per task reveal efficiency and cost regressions, per-tool error rate pinpoints a broken tool, and the rate of hitting the iteration cap shows runaway or stuck loops. E is wrong because the average length of the system prompt is a static configuration property, not a runtime behavior; it says nothing about success, cost per outcome, or reliability (cost is better captured by tokens per task, including cached tokens). Good agent observability is outcome-oriented (success rate, turns to success, cost per success, escalation rate), and averages per call hide the behavior that matters.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuáles son métricas razonables a monitorear para un agente de producción? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Turnos por tarea completada
Fichas y costo por tarea completada
Tasa de error de herramienta por herramienta
Tasa de alcanzar el límite máximo de iteración
Longitud promedio del mensaje del sistema

es.explanation: La observabilidad de los agentes debe estar orientada a los resultados: tasa de éxito, giros hacia el éxito, costo por éxito, tasa de escalada y confiabilidad por herramienta. Los promedios por llamada ocultan el comportamiento que importa.

question: What is the fundamental reason a workflow is easier to evaluate than an agent?

options.text: Workflows use fewer tokens
Each step has a fixed input and output contract, so steps can be tested independently with known expectations
Workflows never fail
Workflows do not use models

explanation: B is correct: a workflow is a predefined path in which each step has a known input and output contract, so you can unit test and evaluate steps independently against expected outputs, and regressions are localized. An agent chooses its own trajectory, so you must evaluate outcomes and trajectories: did it reach a correct result, how efficiently, and did it take unsafe actions, which usually needs curated task sets and graders. A is wrong because token usage is not what determines evaluability (workflows can use more tokens than a short agent run). C is wrong because workflows fail like any LLM system. D is wrong because workflows are typically orchestrated LLM calls; the difference from agents is who controls the flow, not whether models are used.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál es la razón fundamental por la que un flujo de trabajo es más fácil de evaluar que un agente?

options.text: Los flujos de trabajo utilizan menos tokens
Cada paso tiene un contrato fijo de entrada y salida, por lo que los pasos se pueden probar de forma independiente con expectativas conocidas.
Los flujos de trabajo nunca fallan
Los flujos de trabajo no utilizan modelos.

es.explanation: Para los agentes, se deben evaluar trayectorias en lugar de pasos: ¿alcanzó un resultado correcto, con qué eficiencia y tomó acciones inseguras? Esto es más difícil de automatizar y necesita conjuntos de tareas seleccionadas.

question: A request includes tools and the response has stop_reason='end_turn' with only a text block. What does this mean?

options.text: The model answered directly without needing any tool
The tools were malformed and silently ignored
The tools were executed server-side already
The request failed

explanation: A is correct: stop_reason 'end_turn' with only a text block means the model decided it could answer without calling a tool, since with the default tool_choice of auto, tool use is optional. A tool call would have shown stop_reason 'tool_use' with a tool_use block. B is wrong because malformed tool definitions produce a 400 validation error rather than being silently ignored. C is wrong because client tools are executed by your code, never server-side, and server tools produce their own result blocks in the response. D is wrong because a failed request returns an HTTP error, not a successful response with a stop_reason. If you need a tool call, set tool_choice to 'any' or a specific tool; if the model skips tools it should use, improve the tool descriptions and the prompt.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Tool use (function calling)

es.question: Una solicitud incluye herramientas y la respuesta tiene stop_reason='end_turn' con solo un bloque de texto. ¿Qué quiere decir esto?

options.text: El modelo respondió directamente sin necesidad de ninguna herramienta.
Las herramientas estaban mal formadas y se ignoraron silenciosamente.
Las herramientas ya se ejecutaron en el lado del servidor.
La solicitud falló

es.explanation: Si necesita una llamada de herramienta, garantice que configure 'tool_choice' para que requiera una. Si el modelo omite herramientas cuando debería usarlas, la causa habitual es una descripción vaga de la herramienta o un mensaje que no establece cuándo las herramientas son apropiadas.

question: Which are correct approaches to handling concurrency when many agent sessions run simultaneously? Select all that apply.

options.text: A shared rate limiter or token bucket that shapes outbound request rate below the organization limit
A queue with bounded concurrency rather than unbounded parallel dispatch
Backoff with jitter so retries do not synchronize across workers
Letting every worker retry immediately on 429
Per-tenant quotas so one tenant cannot starve others

explanation: The model API is a shared, limited downstream dependency. A is correct because a shared token bucket keeps total outbound rate under the organization's limit instead of relying on 429s. B is correct because bounded concurrency queues smooth bursts and prevent unbounded parallel dispatch. C is correct because exponential backoff with jitter prevents synchronized retry storms (the thundering herd). E is correct because per-tenant quotas enforce fairness so one noisy tenant cannot consume the whole limit. D is wrong because immediate retries on 429 add load exactly when the API is asking you to slow down, worsen throttling, and ignore the retry-after header. These are ordinary distributed systems disciplines applied to the API.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuáles son los enfoques correctos para manejar la concurrencia cuando muchas sesiones de agentes se ejecutan simultáneamente? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Un limitador de tasa compartido o depósito de tokens que determina la tasa de solicitudes salientes por debajo del límite de la organización.
Una cola con simultaneidad limitada en lugar de envío paralelo ilimitado
Retroceda con jitter para que los reintentos no se sincronicen entre los trabajadores
Permitir que todos los trabajadores vuelvan a intentarlo inmediatamente en 429
Cuotas por inquilino para que un inquilino no pueda matar de hambre a otros

es.explanation: Trate la API del modelo como una dependencia descendente limitada y compartida: dé forma a la tasa, limite la concurrencia, agite los reintentos y aplique la equidad. Estas son disciplinas ordinarias de sistemas distribuidos.

question: An application stores conversations and replays them to the API on resumption six months later, but the pinned model is retired. What is the correct preparation?

options.text: Store the model identifier with each conversation and have a documented migration path plus evals to validate the replacement
Assume the API will transparently map retired models to successors
Never pin a model so retirement cannot affect you
Delete conversations older than the model's lifetime

explanation: A is correct: pinned models are retired on a published schedule, so you should record the model identifier with each stored conversation, track deprecation notices, keep a documented migration path, and validate the successor with your eval suite before the deadline (rolling forward behind a flag). Replaying old conversations on a different model can change behavior, so evals matter. B is wrong because the API does not transparently remap retired models; requests to a retired model fail. C is wrong because unpinned aliases move to new versions without notice and can silently change behavior in production, which is worse than a planned migration. D is wrong because deleting conversations destroys user data to avoid an engineering task and is unnecessary, since conversations are plain messages that can be replayed on a successor.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Una aplicación almacena conversaciones y las reproduce en la API cuando se reanuda seis meses después, pero el modelo anclado se retira. ¿Cuál es la preparación correcta?

options.text: Almacene el identificador del modelo con cada conversación y tenga una ruta de migración documentada más evaluaciones para validar el reemplazo.
Suponga que la API asignará de forma transparente los modelos retirados a sus sucesores
Nunca fijes un modelo para que la jubilación no te afecte
Eliminar conversaciones anteriores a la vida útil del modelo

es.explanation: La gestión del ciclo de vida del modelo significa fijar explícitamente, registrar lo que se utilizó, observar los avisos de desuso, evaluar los sucesores de su suite antes de la fecha límite y avanzar detrás de una bandera.

question: Which describes correct handling of the Anthropic beta header?

options.text: It opts a request into a beta feature and should be used deliberately with awareness that beta behavior can change
It is required on every request
It selects the model version
It disables rate limits

explanation: A is correct: the anthropic-beta header opts a request into specific beta features, and beta behavior may change or be withdrawn, so use it deliberately, isolate beta-dependent code, and keep a non-beta fallback where feasible. B is wrong because it is not required on regular requests, only the anthropic-version header is required, and beta headers are only for features in beta. C is wrong because the model is selected by the 'model' parameter in the request body, and the anthropic-version header pins the API version. D is wrong because beta headers do not alter rate limits; limits are governed by your organization's tier and usage.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe el manejo correcto del encabezado beta de Anthropic?

options.text: Opta una solicitud por una función beta y debe usarse deliberadamente teniendo en cuenta que el comportamiento beta puede cambiar.
Se requiere en cada solicitud.
Selecciona la versión del modelo.
Desactiva los límites de tarifas

es.explanation: Aísle las partes del código dependientes de la versión beta y mantenga un respaldo no beta cuando sea posible, ya que las interfaces beta pueden cambiar o retirarse entre versiones.

question: A client sends a request with 188,000 input tokens and max_tokens of 8,000 against a model with a 200,000 token window. What happens?

options.text: The request succeeds because 196,000 is within the window
The request fails because max_tokens cannot exceed 4,096
The input is truncated to fit
The output is capped at 200,000 - 188,000 / 2

explanation: A is correct: the check is input_tokens + max_tokens <= context window, and 188,000 + 8,000 = 196,000, which is under 200,000, so the request is accepted. B is wrong because max_tokens is limited by the model's maximum output (much higher than 4,096 on current models), not by a fixed 4,096 cap. C is wrong because the API does not silently truncate input; if input plus max_tokens exceeded the window it would return a validation error. D is wrong because the output is bounded by max_tokens and the stop conditions, not by a formula like that. With large inputs, lower max_tokens in advance (and count tokens with the token counting endpoint) rather than discovering the limit through an error.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un cliente envía una solicitud con 188 000 tokens de entrada y max_tokens de 8000 frente a un modelo con una ventana de 200 000 tokens. ¿Lo que sucede?

options.text: La solicitud se realiza correctamente porque 196.000 está dentro de la ventana.
La solicitud falla porque max_tokens no puede exceder 4096
La entrada se trunca para ajustarse
La producción tiene un límite de 200.000 - 188.000 / 2

es.explanation: La aritmética a verificar antes de enviar es input_tokens + max_tokens contra la ventana. Cuando las entradas son grandes, reduzca max_tokens en consecuencia en lugar de descubrir el límite mediante un error.

question: Which are valid strategies when a tool must return data that is useful but far too large for context? Select all that apply.

options.text: Write the full data to a file or object store and return the location plus a summary
Return the top N results with a count of what was omitted and a way to request more
Return an aggregate or statistical summary when the agent needs a conclusion rather than raw rows
Return the full payload and rely on the model to ignore what it does not need
Split the payload across multiple tool calls with no indication of continuation

explanation: Ask what decision the agent needs to make and return the minimum information that supports it. A works because the full data goes to a file or object store and the agent gets a location and summary, so it can fetch details selectively. B works because returning the top N with the count omitted and a way to request more (pagination) keeps results bounded while being honest about what is missing. C works because when the agent needs a conclusion, aggregates carry the signal with a tiny fraction of the tokens. D is wrong because large irrelevant payloads waste tokens, dilute attention, can overflow the window, and models do not reliably ignore noise. E is wrong because splitting without any continuation signal leaves the agent unaware that data is missing, so it may conclude from partial data.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuáles son estrategias válidas cuando una herramienta debe devolver datos útiles pero demasiado grandes para el contexto? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Escriba los datos completos en un archivo o almacén de objetos y devuelva la ubicación más un resumen
Devuelve los N resultados principales con un recuento de lo que se omitió y una forma de solicitar más
Devuelve un resumen agregado o estadístico cuando el agente necesita una conclusión en lugar de filas sin procesar.
Devolver la carga útil completa y confiar en el modelo para ignorar lo que no necesita
Divida la carga útil entre múltiples llamadas de herramientas sin indicación de continuación

es.explanation: Pregunte qué decisión debe tomar el agente y luego devuelva la información mínima que respalde esa decisión. Los macrodatos pertenecen a una tienda, no a la ventana contextual.

question: What is the most likely cause of a Claude application producing inconsistent output formats between staging and production?

options.text: Different prompt versions, model identifiers, or sampling parameters between the environments
The API behaves differently by region
Production has more users
Staging uses HTTPS and production does not

explanation: A is correct: when two environments of the same application produce different formats, the first suspects are differences in the effective configuration, namely the prompt version, model identifier (alias vs pinned snapshot), sampling parameters such as temperature, max_tokens, or the tool set. Recording a hash of the effective configuration per request in both environments lets you diff them quickly. B is wrong because the API behavior does not vary by region in a way that changes output format for the same model and inputs. C is wrong because user volume does not change the format of an individual response. D is wrong because TLS only encrypts transport; the API requires HTTPS, and it does not alter content.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la causa más probable de que una aplicación Claude produzca formatos de salida inconsistentes entre la preparación y la producción?

options.text: Diferentes versiones de mensajes, identificadores de modelo o parámetros de muestreo entre los entornos
La API se comporta de manera diferente según la región
La producción tiene más usuarios
La preparación utiliza HTTPS y la producción no.

es.explanation: Bloquee el hash de configuración efectiva (modelo, versión de solicitud, temperatura, max_tokens, conjunto de herramientas) con cada solicitud en ambos entornos. La comparación de dos configuraciones bloqueadas resuelve este tipo de incidente en minutos.

question: Which describes a correct approach to testing code that calls the Claude API?

options.text: Mock the API for unit tests of parsing, retries, and error handling and run a separate eval suite against the real API for quality
Call the real API in every unit test to be realistic
Skip testing because the output is non-deterministic
Assert on exact response strings

explanation: A is correct: use two layers. Unit tests that mock the API are fast, free, and deterministic, and let you cover success, truncation (max_tokens), tool loops, and every error class (429, 529, 500, timeouts) in your parsing, retry and error handling code. A separate eval suite against the real API measures quality and runs when prompts or models change. B is wrong because real calls in every unit test are slow, costly, flaky and non-deterministic, and can hit rate limits in CI. C is wrong because non-determinism is a reason for evals and tolerant assertions, not for skipping tests; your surrounding code is fully testable. D is wrong because exact string assertions are brittle on free-form output; assert on structure, properties or graded criteria instead.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe un enfoque correcto para probar el código que llama a la API de Claude?

options.text: Simule la API para pruebas unitarias de análisis, reintentos y manejo de errores y ejecute un conjunto de evaluación separado contra la API real para mayor calidad.
Llame a la API real en cada prueba unitaria para que sea realista
Omita la prueba porque el resultado no es determinista
Afirmar en cadenas de respuesta exactas

es.explanation: Utilice dos capas: pruebas unitarias rápidas y deterministas con respuestas simuladas que cubren el éxito, el truncamiento, los bucles de herramientas y cada clase de error, y un conjunto de evaluaciones más lento que mide la calidad en llamadas reales ejecutadas en CI en cambios de modelo o aviso.

question: Which fields should be included in a structured log line for each Claude API call? Select all that apply.

options.text: Request ID, model, and prompt version
Input_tokens, output_tokens, and cache token counts
Stop_reason
Latency and whether a retry occurred
The raw API key used

explanation: The per-call log line is the backbone of LLM observability. A (request ID, model, prompt version) lets you trace a call to support with Anthropic and attribute behavior to a configuration. B (input, output and cache token counts from usage) answers cost and cache efficiency questions. C (stop_reason) reveals truncation (max_tokens), refusals, and tool use flow. D (latency and retry flag) covers performance and reliability. E is wrong because logging a raw API key is a security vulnerability: logs are widely accessible and long-lived, so a leaked key grants full account access; log at most a key identifier or last characters. With A to D you can answer cost, quality and reliability questions without extra instrumentation.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué campos deberían incluirse en una línea de registro estructurada para cada llamada a la API de Claude? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: ID de solicitud, modelo y versión del mensaje
Recuentos de tokens de entrada, tokens de salida y tokens de caché
Razón_parada
Latencia y si se produjo un reintento
La clave API sin formato utilizada

es.explanation: Esta línea de registro es la columna vertebral de la observabilidad del LLM. Con él, puede responder preguntas sobre costos, calidad y confiabilidad sin necesidad de instrumentar nada más.

question: A team wants to roll out a new prompt to 5% of traffic and compare outcomes. What must the implementation include?

options.text: Deterministic assignment of users to variants, logging of the variant per request, and a defined outcome metric
Random assignment on every request with no logging
Deploying the new prompt to a separate region
Asking users who they prefer

explanation: A is correct: a canary or A/B rollout needs stable bucketing (assigning each user or session deterministically to a variant so they see a consistent experience), the variant recorded on every request and event, and a predeclared outcome metric (with enough sample size) so the comparison is valid. B is wrong because random per-request assignment without logging makes outcomes impossible to attribute and gives the same user inconsistent behavior. C is wrong because a separate region confounds the experiment with regional differences in traffic and adds infrastructure, and does not by itself give a comparison. D is wrong because asking users for a preference is a weak, biased, low-volume signal compared to measured outcome metrics (and can be a complement, not a mechanism).

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un equipo quiere implementar un nuevo mensaje para el 5 % del tráfico y comparar los resultados. ¿Qué debe incluir la implementación?

options.text: Asignación determinista de usuarios a variantes, registro de la variante por solicitud y una métrica de resultado definida
Asignación aleatoria en cada solicitud sin registro
Implementación del nuevo mensaje en una región separada
Preguntar a los usuarios quién prefieren

es.explanation: Trate los experimentos rápidos como cualquier experimento de producto: agrupación estable por usuario o sesión, variante registrada en cada evento, una métrica principal predeclarada y un plan de tamaño de muestra.

question: What is the correct interpretation of an 'overloaded' error (529)?

options.text: The API is temporarily under heavy load, retry later with backoff
Your request exceeded the context window
Your account is over its spending limit
The model does not exist

explanation: A is correct: HTTP 529 overloaded_error means the API is temporarily under heavy load across users, not a problem with your request, so retry with exponential backoff and jitter, bounded attempts, and a degraded fallback, and alert if it is sustained. B is wrong because exceeding the context window yields a 400 invalid_request_error. C is wrong because spending or usage limits show up as 429 or billing-related errors, not 529. D is wrong because an unknown model returns 404 not_found_error. Treat 529 similarly to 429 and 5xx: they are transient and retryable, unlike 400, 401, 403 and 404, which retries cannot fix.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la interpretación correcta de un error "sobrecargado" (529)?

options.text: La API está temporalmente bajo carga pesada, vuelva a intentarlo más tarde con una pausa
Su solicitud superó la ventana de contexto
Su cuenta ha superado su límite de gasto
El modelo no existe

es.explanation: Maneje 529 como 429 y 500: retroceso exponencial con inquietud, intentos limitados y un retroceso degradado si se agota el presupuesto. Alertar si la tasa es sostenida y no momentánea.

question: Which describes correct multi-tenant isolation for a SaaS product built on Claude?

options.text: Enforce that retrieval and tools only access the requesting tenant's data and never mix tenants content in a single context
Use a separate API key per tenant
Rely on the model not to mention other tenants
Isolate tenants only for paid plans

explanation: A is correct: tenant isolation must be enforced deterministically in the data and tool layers, scoping every retrieval query and tool call to the requesting tenant and never placing multiple tenants' content in one context window, because anything in context can be surfaced by the model, including through prompt injection. Recheck the tenant identifier at the tool boundary and assert it on every returned record. C is wrong because relying on the model not to mention other tenants is a probabilistic instruction, not an access control. D is wrong because isolation is a security requirement for all tenants, not a paid feature. B (a key per tenant) can help with usage attribution and billing, but it does not control what data enters a context, so it does not provide data isolation by itself.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué describe el aislamiento multiinquilino correcto para un producto SaaS basado en Claude?

options.text: Hacer cumplir que la recuperación y las herramientas solo accedan a los datos del inquilino solicitante y nunca mezclen el contenido de los inquilinos en un solo contexto.
Utilice una clave API independiente por inquilino
Confíe en el modelo sin mencionar a otros inquilinos.
Aislar a los inquilinos solo para planes pagos

es.explanation: El alcance del inquilino se debe aplicar en la capa de datos y volver a verificarse en el límite de la herramienta. Incluya el identificador del inquilino en cada consulta de recuperación y aseverelo en cada registro devuelto.

question: Which are correct statements about handling PII in a Claude integration? Select all that apply.

options.text: Minimize what is sent by redacting or tokenizing fields the task does not require
Apply retention limits and access controls to stored prompts and completions
Document the lawful basis and disclose the processing to users where required
Send full records because more context always improves quality
Use meta.user_id to carry the user's real email for traceability

explanation: A, B and C are ordinary data protection applied to LLM features: minimize what you send by redacting or tokenizing fields the task does not need, apply retention limits and access controls to stored prompts and completions (new places where personal data lives), and document the lawful basis and disclose processing where required. D is wrong because sending full records increases privacy exposure and cost, and more context does not always improve quality (irrelevant data can degrade it). E is wrong because the metadata user_id field should be an opaque identifier such as a hash or internal ID; Anthropic's documentation says not to include names, emails or phone numbers in it.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuáles son afirmaciones correctas sobre el manejo de PII en una integración de Claude? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Minimice lo que se envía redactando o tokenizando campos que la tarea no requiere
Aplicar límites de retención y controles de acceso a las indicaciones y finalizaciones almacenadas
Documentar la base legal y divulgar el procesamiento a los usuarios cuando sea necesario.
Envíe registros completos porque más contexto siempre mejora la calidad
Utilice meta.user_id para llevar el correo electrónico real del usuario para su trazabilidad.

es.explanation: La ingeniería de privacidad para las funciones de LLM es principalmente protección de datos ordinaria (minimizar, controlar el acceso, limitar la retención y documentar). La parte novedosa es que las indicaciones y las completaciones son nuevos lugares para los datos personales.

question: A developer wants a single request to both call a tool and produce user-visible commentary. Is this possible?

options.text: Yes, an assistant turn may contain a text block and one or more tool_use blocks
No, tool calls and text are mutually exclusive
Only if streaming is disabled
Only with tool_choice set to none

explanation: A is correct: an assistant message's content is an array of blocks, and the model can emit a text block (commentary or reasoning narration) followed by one or more tool_use blocks in the same turn (stop_reason 'tool_use'). Your UI can render the text to the user while your code executes the tools, and you must return a tool_result for every tool_use. B is wrong because text and tool calls are not mutually exclusive. C is wrong because streaming works with this and delivers text and tool_use blocks as events. D is wrong because tool_choice 'none' prevents tool use entirely, so no tool_use block would be produced.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un desarrollador quiere una única solicitud para llamar a una herramienta y producir comentarios visibles para el usuario. ¿Es esto posible?

options.text: Sí, un turno de asistente puede contener un bloque de texto y uno o más bloques de uso de herramientas.
No, las llamadas a herramientas y los mensajes de texto son mutuamente excluyentes.
Solo si la transmisión está deshabilitada
Sólo con tool_choice establecido en ninguno

es.explanation: Represente los bloques de texto al usuario mientras ejecuta los bloques tool_use en segundo plano. Así es como las IU agentes muestran razonamiento/narración junto con la actividad de la herramienta.

question: What is the most robust way to handle a model returning an enum value outside the allowed set?

options.text: Validate against the allowed set and either retry with a corrective message or route to a defined fallback
Accept it and pass it downstream
Map it to the closest allowed value silently
Raise an unhandled exception

explanation: A is correct: model output is untrusted input, so validate it against the allowed set and then either retry with a corrective message (telling the model what was invalid) or route to a defined fallback. B is wrong because passing an invalid value downstream can corrupt data or trigger undefined behavior. C is wrong because silently mapping to the nearest value hides errors and can produce plausible but wrong results. D is wrong because an unhandled exception turns a recoverable condition into an outage. Better still, prevent it by declaring the enum in a tool input_schema (and with strict tool use or structured outputs, where available, schema conformance is enforced), which turns the runtime failure into a rarity you still guard against.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la forma más sólida de manejar un modelo que devuelve un valor de enumeración fuera del conjunto permitido?

options.text: Valide con el conjunto permitido y vuelva a intentarlo con un mensaje correctivo o dirija a un respaldo definido
Acéptalo y pásalo aguas abajo.
Asignelo al valor permitido más cercano de forma silenciosa
Generar una excepción no controlada

es.explanation: Mejor aún, evítelo: exprese la enumeración en una herramienta input_schema para que la API la valide, lo que convierte este error de tiempo de ejecución en una imposibilidad.

question: Which architectural property makes horizontal scaling of a Claude backend service straightforward?

options.text: The Messages API is stateless, so any instance can serve any request given the conversation from your data store
The API maintains sticky sessions per client
Responses are cached globally by the provider for all customers
Rate limits are per instance

explanation: A is correct: the Messages API is stateless, so every request carries the full conversation and any instance can serve any request as long as it can load the conversation from your data store; the state to scale is your own conversation store and rate limit coordination. B is wrong because the API has no sticky sessions or server-side conversation memory for the standard Messages API. C is wrong because responses are not cached across customers (prompt caching is a per-organization prefix cache for inputs and does not return stored answers). D is wrong because rate limits are applied per organization (and model/tier), not per instance, so you need shared coordination across instances.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué propiedad arquitectónica hace que el escalamiento horizontal de un servicio backend de Claude sea sencillo?

options.text: La API de mensajes no tiene estado, por lo que cualquier instancia puede atender cualquier solicitud dada la conversación de su almacén de datos.
La API mantiene sesiones fijas por cliente.
El proveedor almacena en caché las respuestas globalmente para todos los clientes.
Los límites de tarifas son por instancia

es.explanation: El estado que debes escalar es tu propio almacén de conversaciones y cualquier coordinación que limite la velocidad. El modelo API en sí no impone requisitos de afinidad.

question: Which of these should trigger an alert in a production Claude integration? Select all that apply.

options.text: Sustained rise in the rate of stop_reason='max_tokens'
A sudden drop in cache hit rate
A spike in tool error rate for a specific tool
Any single 429 response
A sharp increase in tokens per request

explanation: Alert on trends and rates that expose silent regressions. A is right because a sustained rise in stop_reason 'max_tokens' means responses are being truncated, often from prompt or input changes. B is right because a cache hit rate drop usually means a prefix changed (for example non-deterministic serialization) and cost and latency will rise. C is right because a tool error spike points at a broken dependency or schema. E is right because a sharp jump in tokens per request signals prompt bloat or runaway context and a cost regression. D is wrong because an isolated 429 is a normal transient event handled by retry with backoff; alert on a sustained rate of 429s or exhausted retry budgets, not each single occurrence.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál de estos debería activar una alerta en una integración de producción de Claude? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Aumento sostenido de la tasa de stop_reason='max_tokens'
Una caída repentina en la tasa de aciertos de la caché
Un aumento en la tasa de error de la herramienta para una herramienta específica
Cualquier respuesta 429
Un fuerte aumento en tokens por solicitud

es.explanation: Alerta sobre tendencias y tasas, no sobre eventos transitorios individuales. Las alertas de mayor valor son aquellas que detectan regresiones silenciosas de calidad y costos en lugar de fallas ruidosas que notaría de todos modos.

question: Why should the tools array be identical and consistently ordered across requests in caching-sensitive applications?

options.text: Because tool definitions are part of the cacheable prefix and any reordering or change invalidates the cache
Because the model calls tools in array order
Because the API rejects reordered tools
Because ordering determines tool priority

explanation: A is correct: prompt caching works on an exact prefix match, and the cache prefix is built in order of tools, then system, then messages. Any change to tool definitions, including reordering or different key order in serialized JSON, changes the prefix and invalidates the cached content, so you pay full price and latency again. Serialize tools deterministically (sort keys, fixed order). B is wrong because the model does not call tools in array order; it chooses based on the request and descriptions. C is wrong because the API accepts any order. D is wrong because array position does not set priority; steer choice with descriptions and tool_choice.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Por qué la matriz de herramientas debería ser idéntica y estar ordenada de manera consistente en todas las solicitudes en aplicaciones sensibles al almacenamiento en caché?

options.text: Porque las definiciones de herramientas son parte del prefijo almacenable en caché y cualquier reordenamiento o cambio invalida el caché
Porque el modelo llama a las herramientas en orden de matriz.
Porque la API rechaza herramientas reordenadas
Porque el pedido determina la prioridad de la herramienta

es.explanation: Serializar definiciones de herramientas de forma determinista, por ejemplo ordenando claves. La serialización JSON no determinista es una causa común y desconcertante de errores de caché.

question: A repository has a large CLAUDE.md containing the full API documentation for its dependencies. What is the likely problem?

options.text: It consumes substantial context on every session, crowding out the task at hand with information that is mostly irrelevant
Claude Code cannot read files over a certain size
It will cause authentication failures
It disables hooks

explanation: A is correct: CLAUDE.md is loaded into context at the start of every session, so a large file full of dependency documentation consumes a lot of context window and tokens on every task, crowding out relevant material and diluting the instructions that matter. Keep it to durable high-value facts (commands, layout, conventions) and put documentation in files the agent reads on demand, or reference it, or expose it through an MCP documentation server. B is wrong because Claude Code can read large files; the issue is cost and dilution, not a hard limit. C is wrong because file size has no bearing on authentication. D is wrong because CLAUDE.md content does not disable hooks, which are configured in settings.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

es.question: Un repositorio tiene un CLAUDE.md grande que contiene la documentación API completa para sus dependencias. ¿Cuál es el problema probable?

options.text: Consume un contexto sustancial en cada sesión, desplazando la tarea en cuestión con información que es en su mayor parte irrelevante.
Claude Code no puede leer archivos de un tamaño determinado
Provocará fallos de autenticación.
Desactiva los ganchos

es.explanation: Mantenga CLAUDE.md con hechos, comandos, convenciones de diseño y referencias genéricas del proyecto duraderos y de alto valor. La documentación pertenece a archivos que el agente puede leer bajo demanda o en un servidor de documentación MCP.

question: Which are appropriate uses of Claude Code hooks? Select all that apply.

options.text: Running a formatter or linter automatically after file edits
Blocking edits to protected paths such as secrets or infrastructure directories
Emitting a notification or log entry when a session completes
Rewriting the model's reasoning to be more accurate
Validating a command against policy before it executes

explanation: Hooks are shell commands or handlers that Claude Code runs deterministically at lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, Notification and others), so they enforce behavior rather than merely suggest it. A is right: a PostToolUse hook can run a formatter or linter after edits. B is right: a PreToolUse hook can block edits to protected paths by exiting with a blocking status. C is right: Stop or Notification hooks can log or notify on completion. E is right: a PreToolUse hook can validate commands against policy before execution. D is wrong because hooks run outside the model and cannot rewrite its reasoning. Anything that must be guaranteed belongs in a hook (or permissions) rather than in CLAUDE.md, which is advisory.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuáles son los usos apropiados de los ganchos del Código Claude? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Ejecutar un formateador o linter automáticamente después de editar archivos
Bloquear ediciones en rutas protegidas, como secretos o directorios de infraestructura
Emitir una notificación o entrada de registro cuando se completa una sesión
Reescribir el razonamiento del modelo para que sea más preciso.
Validar un comando según la política antes de que se ejecute

es.explanation: Los ganchos le brindan control determinista en puntos definidos del ciclo de vida del agente. Todo lo que debe garantizarse en lugar de fomentarse pertenece a un gancho y no a CLAUDE.md.

question: A team's eval suite shows 92% pass but users complain. Which explanation is most likely?

options.text: The eval set does not reflect the real input distribution, so the 8% failures concentrate in common user scenarios
The model has degraded
92% is simply a low score
Users are wrong

explanation: A is correct: a high pass rate only means something relative to what the eval set measures. If the set does not reflect the real input distribution (too easy, too synthetic, missing common scenarios), the 8% failures can concentrate in exactly the cases users hit most, and the score misleads. Fix it by sampling real production traffic, weighting by frequency and cost of error, and adding every reported failure. B is wrong because a model degradation would also show up in a representative eval, and nothing here suggests it. C is wrong because 92% is not inherently low; the number is meaningless without coverage. D is wrong because user complaints are signal to be investigated, not noise.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: La suite de evaluación de un equipo muestra un 92% de aprobación, pero los usuarios se quejan. ¿Qué explicación es más probable?

options.text: El conjunto de evaluación no refleja la distribución de entrada real, por lo que el 8% de las fallas se concentran en escenarios de usuario comunes.
El modelo se ha degradado
92% es simplemente una puntuación baja
Los usuarios se equivocan.

es.explanation: Muestra de tráfico de producción real para crear y actualizar el conjunto de evaluación. Pondere los casos por frecuencia y por costo del error, y agregue cada falla reportada. Una suite de evaluación que nunca cambia deja de reflejar la realidad.

question: An agent task costs $0.40 per completion, of which 85% is input tokens dominated by recent conversation history and tool definitions. Which two changes have the most impact? Select all that apply.

options.text: Prompt caching the system prompt and tool definitions
Compacting conversation history so old turns are summarized rather than replayed verbatim
Reducing max_tokens
Switching to streaming
Increasing temperature

explanation: When 85% of cost is input tokens made of tool definitions, the system prompt and replayed history, optimize the input. A is right: prompt caching the stable prefix (system prompt and tools) makes repeated reads cost a fraction of the base input price and cuts latency. B is right: compacting old turns into summaries shrinks the volume of tokens replayed on each request, and it also helps reasoning quality. C is wrong because max_tokens only caps output, which is the small 15% share, and does not reduce input. D is wrong because streaming changes how output is delivered (perceived latency), not token cost. E is wrong because temperature affects randomness, not token counts, and would not cut cost. Profile first: when output dominates, concise output and tighter caps are the levers.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Una tarea de agente cuesta 0,40 dólares por finalización, de los cuales el 85% son tokens de entrada dominados por el historial de conversaciones recientes y definiciones de herramientas. ¿Cuáles dos cambios tienen el mayor impacto? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Solicitud de almacenamiento en caché de las definiciones de herramientas y avisos del sistema
Compactar el historial de conversaciones para que los viejos giros se resuman en lugar de reproducirse palabra por palabra
Reducir max_tokens
Cambiar a transmisión
Temperatura creciente

es.explanation: Siempre perfile antes de optimizar. Cuando domina la entrada, el almacenamiento en caché y la compactación del contexto son las palancas; cuando domina la producción, lo son la concisión y los límites de tokens más estrictos.

question: Which describes the correct decision process for enabling extended thinking on a feature?

options.text: Run the eval suite with and without it, compare accuracy against the added latency and cost, then decide per task type
Enable it globally because reasoning helps
Enable it only when max_tokens is small
Enable it whenever tools are in use

explanation: A is correct: extended thinking trades latency and cost (thinking tokens are billed as output tokens) for accuracy on complex reasoning, and the benefit varies by task, so run your eval suite with and without it, weigh gains against added latency and cost, and enable it per task type. B is wrong because enabling it globally pays the cost on simple tasks where it adds nothing. C is wrong because a small max_tokens is the opposite of what thinking needs: the budget_tokens must be less than max_tokens and max_tokens must cover thinking plus the answer, otherwise output is truncated. D is wrong because using tools is not a criterion by itself; whether thinking helps depends on task difficulty (it can help tool-use planning, and has constraints with tool_choice).

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál describe el proceso de decisión correcto para permitir un pensamiento amplio sobre una característica?

options.text: Ejecute el conjunto de evaluación con y sin él, compare la precisión con la latencia y el costo agregados y luego decida por tipo de tarea.
Habilítelo globalmente porque el razonamiento ayuda
Habilítelo solo cuando max_tokens sea pequeño
Habilítelo siempre que haya herramientas en uso.

es.explanation: Cuando lo habilites, dimensiona max_tokens para cubrir el presupuesto de pensamiento más la respuesta esperada o verás el truncamiento inmediatamente.

question: What is the practical meaning of effective context being smaller than the nominal window?

options.text: Model attention degrades as the window fills, so accuracy on details buried in a very long context is lower than on a short one
The API reserves part of the window for internal use
Tokens beyond a threshold are billed but discarded
The window shrinks over the course of a conversation

explanation: A is correct: the nominal window is the maximum that fits, but model attention and retrieval accuracy degrade as the window fills (long-context effects such as details getting missed in the middle), so details buried in a very long context are recalled less reliably than in a short one. That is why context curation beats maximization: keep it lean, put key material at the start and end, and verify with evals. B is wrong because the full window is available for input plus output, though max_tokens must still fit. C is wrong because you are billed for processed tokens, and none are silently discarded; over-limit requests error. D is wrong because the window size is fixed per model; what grows is the content using it.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es el significado práctico de que el contexto efectivo sea más pequeño que la ventana nominal?

options.text: La atención del modelo se degrada a medida que la ventana se llena, por lo que la precisión de los detalles ocultos en un contexto muy largo es menor que en uno corto.
La API reserva parte de la ventana para uso interno.
Los tokens que superan un umbral se facturan pero se descartan
La ventana se reduce durante el transcurso de una conversación.

es.explanation: Esta es la razón por la que la curación del contexto supera a la maximización del contexto: coloque el material más importante al principio y al final, mantenga el total magro y verifique con evaluaciones en lugar de asumir una ventana grande de recuperación de guardados.

question: Which comparison correctly characterizes batch versus synchronous processing?

options.text: Batch trades completion latency for a lower per-token price and is suited to offline workloads
Batch is faster and cheaper in all respects
Batch supports streaming
Batch requests bypass the context window

explanation: A is correct: the Message Batches API processes requests asynchronously (most batches finish within an hour, with a 24-hour maximum) at a 50% discount on token prices, which suits offline work such as evals, enrichment and backfills. B is wrong because batch is cheaper but slower, with no latency guarantee, so it is unsuitable for interactive use. C is wrong because batch results are returned when the job completes, not streamed. D is wrong because batch requests are subject to the same context window limits per request. A mature system routes by urgency, using synchronous streaming for user-facing paths and batch for the rest, and caching works with both.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué comparación caracteriza correctamente el procesamiento por lotes versus el procesamiento sincrónico?

options.text: El lote intercambia la latencia de finalización por un precio por token más bajo y es adecuado para cargas de trabajo fuera de línea.
El lote es más rápido y más barato en todos los aspectos.
El lote admite la transmisión
Las solicitudes por lotes omiten la ventana contextual

es.explanation: Un sistema maduro enruta por urgencia: las rutas orientadas al usuario usan transmisión sincrónica, el enriquecimiento/evaluaciones/rellenos usan lotes. Se aplican las mismas indicaciones y estrategias de almacenamiento en caché a ambos.

question: A feature currently uses a large model with a 300 token output. Cost per request is dominated by output. Which changes reduce cost most? Select all that apply.

options.text: Evaluate a smaller model since the per output token rate is lower
Instruct the model to omit preamble and closing summaries
Tighten max_tokens to the realistic maximum for the task
Enable prompt caching
Increase the number of examples in the prompt

explanation: When output tokens dominate cost (which are priced several times higher than input), reduce output volume or its unit price. A is right: a smaller model has a lower per-output-token rate, and it should be validated with evals. B is right: removing preamble and closing summaries cuts generated tokens without losing content. C is right: tightening max_tokens bounds worst-case output and cost, as long as it stays above the realistic maximum to avoid truncation. D is wrong because prompt caching discounts repeated input, which is not where the cost is. E is wrong because more examples increase input tokens and do not shrink output. Check the input versus output split in the usage object before choosing an optimization.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Actualmente, una función utiliza un modelo grande con una salida de 300 tokens. El costo por solicitud está dominado por la producción. ¿Qué cambios reducen más los costos? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Evalúe un modelo más pequeño ya que la tasa de token por salida es menor
Indique al modelo que omita el preámbulo y los resúmenes finales.
Ajuste max_tokens al máximo realista para la tarea
Habilitar el almacenamiento en caché de avisos
Aumentar el número de ejemplos en el mensaje.

es.explanation: Diagnostique la división de entrada versus salida del objeto de uso antes de elegir una optimización. La aplicación del almacenamiento en caché a una carga de trabajo dominada por los resultados produce resultados decepcionantes y un desperdicio de ingeniería.

question: Which statement about model deprecation is correct?

options.text: Pinned models are eventually retired, so applications need a monitored migration path with evals to validate the successor
Pinned models are supported indefinitely
Deprecation is irrelevant if you use aliases
Deprecated models continue to work but return warnings only

explanation: A is correct: Anthropic publishes deprecation and retirement schedules; after the retirement date, requests to a retired model fail, so you need a monitored migration path and evals to validate the successor before the deadline. The healthy pattern is to pin explicitly, track deprecation notices, keep evals ready, and treat migration as scheduled work. B is wrong because pinned snapshots are not supported indefinitely. C is wrong because aliases point to the latest snapshot and can change behavior without notice, so they do not make deprecation irrelevant; they trade stability for automatic change. D is wrong because after retirement the model stops working and returns errors, rather than only warnings.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué afirmación sobre la desaprobación del modelo es correcta?

options.text: Los modelos fijados eventualmente se retiran, por lo que las aplicaciones necesitan una ruta de migración monitoreada con evaluaciones para validar al sucesor.
Los modelos fijados se admiten indefinidamente
La desaprobación es irrelevante si usa alias
Los modelos obsoletos continúan funcionando pero solo devuelven advertencias

es.explanation: El patrón saludable es: fijar explícitamente, suscribirse a avisos de obsolescencia, mantener listo un conjunto de evaluaciones y tratar la migración como una tarea rutinaria y programada en lugar de una emergencia.

question: What is the primary reason to measure P95 latency rather than only the mean?

options.text: The mean hides a long tail, and users experience the tail as the product being slow or broken
P95 is cheaper to compute
The mean is not supported by monitoring tools
P95 equals the mean for LLM workloads

explanation: A is correct: LLM latency distributions have a long tail driven mostly by output length, queueing and retries; the mean averages away slow outliers, but users experience the slow requests as the product being slow or broken, so P95 (and P99) capture the experience that matters. B is wrong because computing percentiles is not meaningfully cheaper than computing a mean. C is wrong because monitoring tools support means; the issue is what the metric hides. D is wrong because P95 is by definition larger than the mean in a skewed distribution. Because output length drives the tail, concise bounded output formats and max_tokens limits are prompting levers to compress it.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es la razón principal para medir la latencia de P95 en lugar de solo la media?

options.text: La media esconde una cola larga, y los usuarios sienten que la cola es un producto lento o roto.
P95 es más barato de calcular
La media no está respaldada por herramientas de seguimiento.
P95 es igual a la media para las cargas de trabajo de LLM

es.explanation: La longitud de salida es el principal impulsor de la cola. Por lo tanto, la latencia de cola es en parte un problema provocador: los formatos de salida concisos y acotados comprimen la distribución con tanta eficacia como los cambios de infraestructura.

question: Which factors should inform whether to use retrieval augmentation instead of a long context? Select all that apply.

options.text: The corpus is far larger than any context window
Only a small fraction of the corpus is relevant to any given query
Cost per query must stay low at high volume
The corpus is small, static, and fully relevant to every query
Sources must be cited and traced

explanation: Retrieval fits when the corpus cannot or should not fit in context. A is right: a corpus far larger than any window cannot be loaded. B is right: if only a small fraction is relevant per query, loading everything wastes tokens and dilutes attention. C is right: at high volume, sending only relevant passages costs far less per query than a full corpus each time (though prompt caching can offset this for a static corpus). E is right: retrieval gives you identifiable source chunks that can be cited and traced. D is wrong because a small, static corpus fully relevant to every query is the case for long context (ideally cached), where retrieval adds complexity and recall risk. The two are complementary: retrieve candidates, then reason over them in a well-structured long prompt.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Qué factores deberían informar si se debe utilizar el aumento de recuperación en lugar de un contexto largo? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: El corpus es mucho más grande que cualquier ventana de contexto.
Sólo una pequeña fracción del corpus es relevante para cualquier consulta determinada.
El costo por consulta debe mantenerse bajo en grandes volúmenes
El corpus es pequeño, estático y totalmente relevante para cada consulta.
Las fuentes deben citarse y rastrearse.

es.explanation: La recuperación y el contexto largo son complementarios: un diseño común recupera pasajes candidatos y luego los coloca en un contexto largo bien estructurado, ganando tanto selectividad como razonamiento coherente sobre la selección.

question: A model change improves accuracy by 2% but increases P95 latency from 1.2s to 4.5s on an interactive feature. What is the correct analysis?

options.text: Weigh the accuracy gain against the user experience cost and consider routing so only hard cases pay the latency penalty
Always take the accuracy improvement
Always keep the faster model
Latency does not matter if accuracy improves

explanation: A is correct: this is a trade-off to quantify rather than a rule. A 2% accuracy gain may or may not justify a 3.7x increase in P95 latency (1.2s to 4.5s, a 3.3 second increase) on an interactive feature, where latency affects engagement and abandonment. Estimate what the error reduction saves versus what the added latency costs, and consider routing so only hard cases go to the slower model, which usually captures most of the accuracy gain with a fraction of the latency cost. B, C and D are wrong because each applies an absolute rule (always accuracy, always speed, latency irrelevant) that ignores the specific product context and the available middle path.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: Un cambio de modelo mejora la precisión en un 2 % pero aumenta la latencia de P95 de 1,2 segundos a 4,5 segundos en una función interactiva. ¿Cuál es el análisis correcto?

options.text: Sopese la ganancia en precisión con el costo de la experiencia del usuario y considere el enrutamiento para que solo los casos difíciles paguen la penalización por latencia.
Siempre tome la mejora de la precisión
Mantenga siempre el modelo más rápido
La latencia no importa si la precisión mejora

es.explanation: Cuantifique ambos lados: ¿qué ahorra una reducción de errores del 2% y cuánto cuesta un aumento de latencia de 3,3 segundos en participación o abandono? El enrutamiento normalmente captura la mayor parte de la ganancia de precisión a una fracción del costo de latencia.

question: A prompt asks for a summary and receives outputs ranging from one sentence to 12 paragraphs. What is the fix?

options.text: Specify the exact length, structure, and audience, and show one example of the target output
Lower the temperature
Set max_tokens to a small value
Switch to a larger model

explanation: A is correct: wide variance in output length means the prompt leaves length, structure and audience unspecified. Make requirements measurable (a number of sentences or bullets, required sections, what to exclude, who the reader is) and include an example of the target output, which communicates the format more concretely than prose. B is wrong because lowering temperature reduces randomness but does not specify what to produce, so an underspecified prompt can still vary. C is wrong because a small max_tokens would truncate outputs abruptly mid-sentence rather than make them concise; the model does not plan around it. D is wrong because a larger model does not resolve ambiguity in instructions and costs more.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un mensaje solicita un resumen y recibe resultados que van desde una oración hasta 12 párrafos. ¿Cuál es la solución?

options.text: Especifique la duración, la estructura y la audiencia exactas, y muestre un ejemplo del resultado objetivo.
bajar la temperatura
Establecer max_tokens en un valor pequeño
Cambiar a un modelo más grande

es.explanation: Las instrucciones de formato deben ser mensurables: número de oraciones o viñetas, secciones requeridas y qué excluir. Un ejemplo concreta la especificación de una manera que rara vez lo hace la prosa.

question: Which describes an appropriate structure for an agent system prompt?

options.text: Role and objective, available capabilities and when to use them, output and formatting rules, constraints, and how to handle uncertainty and failure
A long unstructured list of everything the agent might encounter
Only the role, leaving everything else to the user turn
The full conversation history

explanation: A is correct: an effective agent system prompt is structured and complete yet as short as possible: the role and objective, the available capabilities and when to use each, the output and formatting rules, the constraints, and how to handle uncertainty and failure (for example ask, escalate, or stop). B is wrong because a long unstructured list of everything possible buries priorities and is hard to maintain and test. C is wrong because a role alone leaves behavior undefined and moves instructions into user turns, where they are less stable and easier to override. D is wrong because conversation history belongs in the messages array, not the system prompt. Rules that must hold absolutely should be enforced in code, not carried by the prompt.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Cuál describe una estructura apropiada para un mensaje de sistema de agente?

options.text: Rol y objetivo, capacidades disponibles y cuándo usarlas, reglas de salida y formato, restricciones y cómo manejar la incertidumbre y el fracaso.
Una lista larga y no estructurada de todo lo que el agente podría encontrar.
Sólo el rol, dejando todo lo demás en manos del usuario.
El historial completo de conversaciones.

es.explanation: Manténgalo estructurado y lo más breve posible mientras esté completo. Mueva los requisitos absolutos a la aplicación a nivel de código para que el mensaje no tenga que contener reglas que no puede garantizar.

question: Which practices support effective context engineering in a long-running agent? Select all that apply.

options.text: Deciding explicitly at each step what belongs in the window and what does not
Summarizing completed phases into structured findings
Re-anchoring the current goal near the end of the prompt
Appending every tool result verbatim for completeness
Storing durable artifacts externally and re-reading them selectively

explanation: Context is a finite working set with a budget, not an append-only log. A is right: decide at each step what belongs in the window. B is right: summarizing completed phases into structured findings keeps the conclusions while dropping the bulk. C is right: restating the current goal near the end of the prompt counters drift in long contexts. E is right: storing durable artifacts (notes, plans, data) outside the context and re-reading them selectively lets work continue past the window and survive context resets. D is wrong because appending every tool result verbatim bloats the window, buries signal, raises cost and degrades reasoning; trim, clear stale tool results, or summarize instead.

source.title: Anthropic Research: Building effective agents

es.question: ¿Qué prácticas respaldan la ingeniería de contexto eficaz en un agente de larga duración? Seleccione todo lo que corresponda.

options.text: Decidir explícitamente en cada paso qué pertenece a la ventana y qué no.
Resumir las fases completadas en hallazgos estructurados
Reanclar el objetivo actual cerca del final del mensaje
Adjuntar cada resultado de la herramienta palabra por palabra para que esté completo
Almacenar artefactos duraderos externamente y releerlos selectivamente

es.explanation: Trate la ventana de contexto como un conjunto de trabajo con un presupuesto, no como un registro de solo agregar. Lo que omites importa tanto como lo que pones.

question: Why does asking for reasoning inside tagged tags help downstream systems?

options.text: It allows code to extract the final answer cleanly without parsing the reasoning text
It reduces the number of reasoning tokens
It hides the reasoning from billing
It prevents the model from reasoning incorrectly

explanation: A is correct: asking the model to put reasoning in one tag (such as <thinking>) and the final answer in another (such as <answer>) lets your code extract the answer block reliably with a simple parse, so verbose or exploratory reasoning never contaminates what downstream systems consume. B is wrong because tags do not shorten reasoning; they organize it. C is wrong because all generated tokens are billed whether or not they are tagged. D is wrong because structure does not guarantee correct reasoning; it only makes the output parseable. Using XML tags to separate parts of a response is a core Anthropic prompt engineering technique.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Por qué pedir razonamiento dentro de las etiquetas etiquetadas ayuda a los sistemas posteriores?

options.text: Permite que el código extraiga la respuesta final de forma limpia sin analizar el texto de razonamiento.
Reduce la cantidad de fichas de razonamiento.
Oculta el razonamiento de la facturación.
Evita que el modelo razone incorrectamente.

es.explanation: El patrón es razonar en un bloque de etiquetas y responder en otro. Su código lee solo el bloque de respuestas, por lo que el razonamiento detallado o exploratorio nunca contamina la salida que consumen sus sistemas.

question: A retrieval-augmented prompt includes 10 passages, three of which are relevant. What most improves answer quality?

options.text: Improving retrieval precision so fewer irrelevant passages are included and asking the model to cite which passages it used
Including 20 passages instead so the relevant ones are certainly present
Removing all passages and relying on model knowledge
Increasing max_tokens

explanation: A is correct: with 3 relevant of 10 passages, the noise comes from low retrieval precision. Improving precision (better embeddings, reranking, a tighter top-k, filtering) reduces distraction, and asking the model to cite which passages it used makes answers verifiable and grounded. B is wrong because 20 passages would add more irrelevant material, increasing noise and cost, and relevance would still not be guaranteed. C is wrong because dropping retrieval removes the grounding and invites hallucination or outdated information. D is wrong because max_tokens only caps output length and does not affect answer quality. Retrieval quality usually matters more than prompt wording in RAG, so measure retriever precision and recall separately from end-to-end quality.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: Un mensaje de recuperación aumentada incluye 10 pasajes, tres de los cuales son relevantes. ¿Qué es lo que más mejora la calidad de las respuestas?

options.text: Mejorar la precisión de la recuperación para que se incluyan menos pasajes irrelevantes y pedirle al modelo que cite qué pasajes utilizó.
Incluyendo 20 pasajes en su lugar para que los relevantes estén ciertamente presentes.
Eliminar todos los pasajes y confiar en el conocimiento del modelo.
Incrementando max_tokens

es.explanation: La calidad de la recuperación suele ser más importante que la pronta redacción en los sistemas RAG. Mida la precisión y la recuperación del recuperador por separado de la calidad de la respuesta de un extremo a otro para saber qué componente reparar.

question: What is a risk of relying on a single very long prompt to encode all business rules for a complex domain?

options.text: Adherence becomes inconsistent as rules multiply and the prompt becomes hard to test, version, and reason about
The prompt cannot exceed 4,000 tokens
Long prompts cannot be cached
The model will refuse to answer

explanation: A is correct: when one huge prompt encodes all business rules, adherence tends to become inconsistent as rules multiply and compete, and the prompt becomes hard to test, version, and reason about because you cannot isolate which rule caused a failure. Decompose: route to specialized prompts per case type, enforce hard rules in code, and keep each prompt focused so each piece can be tested independently. B is wrong because prompts can be far longer than 4,000 tokens. C is wrong because long prompts can be cached, and caching is often useful for them (with a minimum cacheable length). D is wrong because length alone does not make the model refuse.

source.title: Anthropic Docs: Claude developer guide & API reference

es.question: ¿Cuál es el riesgo de depender de un único mensaje muy largo para codificar todas las reglas comerciales de un dominio complejo?

options.text: La adherencia se vuelve inconsistente a medida que las reglas se multiplican y el mensaje se vuelve difícil de probar, versionar y razonar al respecto.
El mensaje no puede exceder los 4000 tokens.
Las indicaciones largas no se pueden almacenar en caché
La modelo se negará a responder
